title.zh: 卷一 宋本紀上第一 武帝 少帝
title.en: Volume 1 Liu Song Annals 1: Emperor Wu, Emperor Shao
title.raw: 卷一 宋本紀上第一 武帝 少帝 Volume 1 Liu Song Annals 1: Emperor Wu, Emperor Shao

sentences.zh: 武帝 少帝

translations.literal: Emperor Wu; Emperor Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu and Emperor Shao.

sentences.zh: 嘗游京口竹林寺，獨臥講堂前，上有五色龍章，眾僧見之，驚以白帝，帝獨喜曰：「上人無妄言。

translations.literal: Once he visited Zhulin Temple in Jingkou and lay alone before the lecture hall; above him was a five-colored dragon pattern. The monks saw it, and in alarm reported it to the Emperor. The Emperor alone was pleased and said, "The master speaks without falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on a visit to Zhulin Temple at Jingkou, he lay alone before the lecture hall. Above him appeared a five-colored dragon pattern. The monks, startled, reported it to him; he alone was pleased and said, "The master speaks no falsehood.

sentences.zh: 」皇考墓在丹徒之候山，其地秦史所謂曲阿、丹徒間有天子氣者也。

translations.literal: " His father's tomb was at Houshan in Dantu—that place of which Qin-era records speak, where between Qu'e and Dantu there was the aura of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " His father's tomb lay at Houshan in Dantu, in the very region that Qin dynasty chronicles described as breathing the aura of an imperial destiny between Qu'e and Dantu.

sentences.zh: 時有孔恭者，妙善占墓，帝嘗與經墓，欺之曰：「此墓何如？

translations.literal: There was one Kong Gong, skilled at divining tombs. The Emperor once passed the tomb with him and deceived him, saying, "What of this tomb?
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Kong Gong who was skilled at reading tombs by divination. The Emperor once passed the tomb with him and put him to the test, asking, "What do you make of this tomb?

sentences.zh: 」孔恭曰：「非常地也。

translations.literal: " Kong Gong said, "It is no ordinary ground.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Gong replied, "This is no ordinary ground.

sentences.zh: 」帝由是益自負。

translations.literal: " From this the Emperor was all the more self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the Emperor grew all the more confident in himself.

sentences.zh: 行止時見二小龍附翼，樵漁山澤，同侶或亦睹焉。

translations.literal: As he went and stopped, he at times saw two small dragons attached to his sides. When he gathered firewood and fished in mountains and marshes, his companions sometimes saw them as well.
translations.idiomatic: As he traveled, he would sometimes see two small dragons flanking his sides. When he gathered firewood or fished in the hills and marshes, his companions sometimes saw them too.

sentences.zh: 及貴，龍形更大。

translations.literal: When he rose to high rank, the dragon forms grew larger.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to high rank, the dragons appeared larger still.

sentences.zh: 帝素貧，時人莫能知，唯琅邪王謐獨深敬焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor had always been poor, and men of the time could not discern his worth—only Wang Mi of Langya alone deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always been poor, and few in his day could see what he would become—only Wang Mi of Langya treated him with deep respect.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗負刁逵社錢三萬，經時無以還，被逵執，謐密以己錢代償，由是得釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor once owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community-district money. After a long time he could not repay it and was seized by Kui. Mi secretly used his own money to repay the debt on his behalf, and thereby the Emperor was released.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community-district funds. Unable to repay after a long while, he was seized by Kui. Mi secretly paid the debt with his own money and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 後伐荻新洲，見大蛇長數丈，射之，傷。

translations.literal: Later, while cutting rushes at Xinzhou, he saw a great snake several zhang long, shot it, and wounded it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while cutting rushes on Xinzhou, he saw a great serpent several zhang in length, shot it, and wounded it.

sentences.zh: 明日復至洲，裏聞有杵臼聲，往覘之，見童子數人皆青衣，於榛中搗藥。

translations.literal: The next day he returned to the islet. Inside he heard the sound of a mortar and pestle, went to look, and saw several youths all in green garments pounding medicine in the hazels.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned to the islet. From within he heard mortar and pestle at work. Going to look, he found several youths in green garments pounding medicine among the hazel thickets.

sentences.zh: 問其故，答曰：「我王為劉寄奴所射，合散傅之。

translations.literal: He asked the reason. They answered, "Our king was shot by Liu Jigong; we are mixing powder to apply to the wound.
translations.idiomatic: He asked what they were doing. They answered, "Our king was shot by Liu Jigong; we are mixing a poultice to dress the wound.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「王神何不殺之？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "If the king is divine, why not kill him?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "If your king is a spirit, why not kill me?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「劉寄奴王者不死，不可殺。

translations.literal: " They answered, "Liu Jigong is a king who cannot die; he cannot be killed.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "Liu Jigong is a king who cannot die. He cannot be killed.

sentences.zh: 」帝叱之，皆散，仍收藥而反。

translations.literal: " The Emperor shouted at them, and they all scattered. He still gathered the medicine and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor shouted at them, and they all vanished. He took the medicine anyway and went back.

sentences.zh: 又經客下邳逆旅，會一沙門謂帝曰：「江表當亂，安之者，其在君乎。

translations.literal: Again, passing a traveler's inn at Xiapi, he met a monk who said to the Emperor, "Turmoil will come to the lands south of the Yangtze. The one who will pacify it—is it not you?
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, stopping at a traveler's inn below Xiapi, he met a monk who told him, "The lands south of the Yangtze will soon fall into turmoil. The one who will restore order—is it not you?

sentences.zh: 」帝先患手創，積年不愈，沙門有一黃藥，因留與帝，既而忽亡，帝以黃散傅之，其創一傅而愈。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had long suffered from a hand wound that for years would not heal. The monk had a yellow medicine and left it with the Emperor, then suddenly vanished. The Emperor applied the yellow powder to the wound, and with one application it healed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor had long suffered from a hand wound that would not heal for years. The monk gave him a yellow salve and then suddenly vanished. He applied the powder once, and the wound healed.

sentences.zh: 寶其餘及所得童子藥，每遇金創，傅之並驗。

translations.literal: He treasured what remained of it and the medicine obtained from the youths. Whenever he met a metal wound, applying it always proved effective.
translations.idiomatic: He kept what remained of that salve, together with the medicine taken from the youths, and whenever he suffered a blade or spear wound, applying it never failed.

sentences.zh: 初為冠軍孫無終司馬。

translations.literal: At first he served as Major under Champion General Sun Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as Major on the staff of Champion General Sun Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 晉隆安三年十一月，祅賊孫恩作亂于會稽，朝廷遣衛將軍謝琰、前將軍劉牢之東討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Long'an of Jin, the demonic rebel Sun En raised rebellion at Kuaiji. The court sent General of the Guard Xie Yan and Forward General Liu Laozhi east to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Long'an, the sorcerer-rebel Sun En rose in rebellion at Kuaiji. The court dispatched General of the Guard Xie Yan and Forward General Liu Laozhi to campaign against him in the east.

sentences.zh: 牢之請帝參府軍事，命與數十人覘賊，遇賊眾數千，帝便與戰，所將人多死，而帝奮長刀，所殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Laozhi requested that the Emperor join headquarters military affairs and ordered him with several tens of men to scout the rebels. They encountered rebel forces numbering in the thousands. The Emperor at once gave battle. Most of the men he led died, but wielding a long blade the Emperor killed and wounded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi asked the Emperor to serve on his staff and sent him with a few dozen men to scout the rebels. They ran into thousands of enemy troops. The Emperor fought at once. Most of his men were killed, but swinging a long blade he cut down a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 牢之子敬宣疑帝為賊所困，乃輕騎尋之；

translations.literal: Laozhi's son Jingxuan suspected that the Emperor had been trapped by the rebels and rode out lightly to find him.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi's son Jingxuan feared the Emperor had been surrounded and rode out with a light escort to find him.

sentences.zh: 既而眾騎並至，遂平山陰，恩遁入海。

translations.literal: Before long all the cavalry arrived together, and they then pacified Shanyin. En fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rest of the cavalry arrived, Shanyin was pacified, and En fled out to sea.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，恩復入會稽，殺謝琰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, En again entered Kuaiji and killed Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year En returned to Kuaiji and killed Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，牢之復東征，使帝戍句章，句章城小人少，帝每戰陷陣，賊乃退還浹口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Laozhi again campaigned east and sent the Emperor to garrison Gouzhang. Gouzhang was a small city with few defenders. The Emperor each time charged into the enemy ranks, and the rebels withdrew to Jiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Laozhi marched east again and posted the Emperor at Gouzhang. Gouzhang was a small city with few defenders, but each time the Emperor broke the enemy line the rebels fell back to Jiakou.

sentences.zh: 時東伐諸將，士卒暴掠，百姓皆苦之，惟帝獨無所犯。

translations.literal: At the time the generals on the eastern campaign let their soldiers plunder violently, and the common people all suffered from it. Only the Emperor's men committed no violations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eastern campaign generals allowed their troops to plunder at will, and the people suffered greatly. Only under the Emperor's command were no outrages committed.

sentences.zh: 五年春，恩頻攻句章，帝屢破之，恩復入海。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year En repeatedly attacked Gouzhang. The Emperor repeatedly defeated him, and En again fled to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year En repeatedly assaulted Gouzhang. The Emperor repulsed him again and again, and En once more fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 三月，恩北出海鹽，帝築城於故海鹽，賊日來攻城，城內兵少，帝乃選敢死士擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month En came north out of Haiyan. The Emperor built a fort at old Haiyan. The rebels came daily to attack the city. With few soldiers inside, the Emperor selected dare-to-die warriors and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month En came north from Haiyan. The Emperor built a fort at old Haiyan. The rebels attacked every day, but with few troops inside the walls he chose dare-to-die warriors and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 時雖連勝，帝深慮眾寡不敵，乃一夜偃旗示以羸弱，觀其懈，乃奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Though he had won repeatedly, the Emperor deeply feared that his numbers were too few to match the enemy. One night he lowered his banners to show weakness; when he saw them slacken, he struck fiercely and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had won repeatedly, the Emperor still feared he could not hold against superior numbers. One night he lowered his banners to feign weakness; when he saw the enemy relax, he charged and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 恩知城不可下，進向滬瀆，帝棄城追之。

translations.literal: En knew the city could not be taken and advanced toward Huddu. The Emperor abandoned the city and pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: En saw the city could not be taken and marched toward Huddu. The Emperor abandoned the fort and pursued.

sentences.zh: 海鹽令鮑陋遣子嗣之以吳兵一千為前驅，帝以吳人不習戰，命之在後，不從。

translations.literal: Bao Lou, magistrate of Haiyan, sent his son Sizhi with one thousand Wu troops as vanguard. The Emperor, judging the men of Wu unskilled in war, ordered them to the rear, but they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Lou, magistrate of Haiyan, sent his son Sizhi ahead with a thousand Wu troops. The Emperor, believing the Wu men poor fighters, ordered them to the rear, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 是夜帝多設奇兵，兼置旗鼓，明日戰，伏發，賊退，嗣之追奔陷沒。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor set many ambush troops and also placed drums and banners. The next day in battle the ambush sprang; the rebels retreated, and Sizhi in pursuit fell into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor laid many ambushes and set drums and banners. When battle came the next day, the trap closed, the rebels fled, and Sizhi's pursuit ended in disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝且退且戰，麾下死傷將盡，乃至向處止，令左右解取死人衣以示暇。

translations.literal: The Emperor fought as he retreated. His followers were nearly all killed or wounded. When he reached the place where he had halted before, he ordered his attendants to strip clothing from the dead to show he was at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fought as he withdrew until his followers were nearly all killed or wounded. When he reached the place where he had halted earlier, he ordered his men to strip clothing from the dead to show he still had time to spare.

sentences.zh: 賊疑尚有伏，乃引去。

translations.literal: The rebels suspected an ambush still remained and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected another ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六月，恩浮海至丹徒，帝兼行與俱至，奔擊大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month En came by sea to Dantu. The Emperor traveled swiftly and arrived together with him, then charged and routed him completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month En came by sea to Dantu. The Emperor marched at speed, caught up with him, charged, and broke him completely.

sentences.zh: 恩至建鄴，知朝廷有備，遂走鬱洲。

translations.literal: En reached Jianye, saw that the court was prepared, and fled to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: En reached Jianye, found the court ready, and fled to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，晉帝以帝為下邳太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Jin Emperor appointed the Emperor Governor of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Jin emperor appointed him Governor of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 帝又追恩至鬱洲及海鹽，頻破之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again pursued En to Yuzhou and Haiyan and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pursued En again to Yuzhou and Haiyan and defeated him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 恩自是饑饉，奔臨海。

translations.literal: En thereafter, stricken by famine, fled to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter En, weakened by famine, fled to Linhai.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，荊州刺史桓玄舉兵東下，驃騎將軍司馬元顯遣牢之拒之，帝又參其軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing, Jingzhou Inspector Huan Xuan raised troops and marched east. Cavalry General Sima Yuansian sent Laozhi to resist him, and the Emperor again joined his military staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing, Jingzhou Inspector Huan Xuan raised an army and marched east. Cavalry General Sima Yuansian sent Laozhi to oppose him, and the Emperor again served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 玄至，帝請擊之，牢之不許，乃遣子敬宣詣玄請和。

translations.literal: When Xuan arrived, the Emperor requested to attack him. Laozhi would not permit it and instead sent his son Jingxuan to Xuan to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan arrived, the Emperor urged an attack. Laozhi refused and sent his son Jingxuan to Xuan to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 帝與東海何無忌並固諫，不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor and He Wuji of Donghai together remonstrated firmly, but Laozhi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and He Wuji of Donghai pleaded with him together, but Laozhi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 玄克建鄴，以牢之為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Xuan took Jianye and made Laozhi Interior Prefect of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan captured Jianye and appointed Laozhi Interior Prefect of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 牢之懼，招帝於廣陵舉兵，帝曰：「人情去矣，廣陵亦豈可得之？

translations.literal: Laozhi grew afraid and summoned the Emperor to Guangling to raise troops. The Emperor said, "Men's hearts have already departed. How could Guangling be taken even then?
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi, afraid, summoned the Emperor to Guangling to raise troops. The Emperor said, "The people's hearts are already gone. Even Guangling could not be held.

sentences.zh: 」牢之竟縊於新洲。

translations.literal: " In the end Laozhi hanged himself at Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Laozhi ended by hanging himself at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 何無忌謂帝曰：「我將何之？

translations.literal: He Wuji said to the Emperor, "Where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji asked the Emperor, "Where am I to go?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「可隨我還京口。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Come back with me to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor answered, "Return with me to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 玄必守臣節，當與卿事之；

translations.literal: Xuan will surely keep the integrity of a minister, and I shall serve him together with you.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan will surely keep faith as a minister, and we can serve him together.

sentences.zh: 不然，與卿圖之。」

translations.literal: If not, then we shall plot against him together."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we shall plot against him together."

sentences.zh: 玄從兄修以撫軍將軍鎮丹徒，以帝為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Xuan's older cousin Xiu, as Pacifying Army General, garrisoned Dantu and made the Emperor Army Headquarters Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's older cousin Xiu, serving as Pacifying Army General at Dantu, appointed the Emperor Army Headquarters Aide.

sentences.zh: 孫恩自敗後，懼見獲，乃投水死於臨海，餘眾推恩妹夫盧循為主。

translations.literal: After Sun En's defeat, fearing capture, he drowned himself at Linhai. The remaining followers made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Sun En, fearing capture, drowned himself at Linhai. The survivors made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader.

sentences.zh: 玄復遣帝東征。

translations.literal: Xuan again sent the Emperor east on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan once more dispatched the Emperor on an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 二年，循奔永嘉，帝追破之。

translations.literal: In the second year Xun fled to Yongjia, and the Emperor pursued and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Lu Xun fled to Yongjia, and the Emperor pursued and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 六月，加帝彭城內史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor was additionally made Interior Prefect of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was additionally appointed Interior Prefect of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，桓玄篡位，遷晉帝于尋陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Huan Xuan usurped the throne and moved the Jin Emperor to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huan Xuan usurped the throne and moved the Jin emperor to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 桓修入朝，帝從至建鄴，玄見帝，謂司徒王謐曰：「昨見劉裕，風骨不恒，蓋人傑也。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu entered court, and the Emperor followed him to Jianye. When Xuan saw the Emperor, he said to Minister over the Masses Wang Mi, "Yesterday I saw Liu Yu. His bearing and bone structure are not ordinary. He is surely a hero among men.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu went to court, and the Emperor followed him to Jianye. When Xuan saw the Emperor, he told Minister over the Masses Wang Mi, "Yesterday I saw Liu Yu. His bearing is unlike that of ordinary men. He is clearly a hero.

sentences.zh: 」每遊集，贈賜甚厚。

translations.literal: " At every gathering and feast he bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: " At every gathering he lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 玄妻劉氏，尚書令耽之女也，聰明有智鑒，嘗見帝，因謂玄曰：「劉裕龍行虎步，視瞻不凡，恐必不為人下，宜早為其所。

translations.literal: Xuan's wife, Lady Liu, was the daughter of Director of the Masters of Writing Dan. Intelligent and discerning, she once saw the Emperor and therefore said to Xuan, "Liu Yu walks like a dragon and steps like a tiger; his gaze is not ordinary. I fear he will surely not remain beneath others. You should deal with him early.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's wife, Lady Liu, was the daughter of Director of the Masters of Writing Dan. Clever and sharp-eyed, she once saw the Emperor and told Xuan, "Liu Yu walks like a dragon and steps like a tiger, and his gaze is not that of an ordinary man. I fear he will never serve under another. You should remove him while you still can.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「我方平蕩中原，非裕莫可，待關、隴平定，然後議之。」

translations.literal: " Xuan said, "I am just now pacifying the Central Plains, and none but Yu can do it. Wait until Guan and Long are settled, and then we shall discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "I am just now pacifying the Central Plains, and none but Yu can serve me there. Wait until Guan and Long are settled, and then we shall discuss it."

sentences.zh: 修尋還京口，帝托以金創疾動，不堪步從，乃與無忌同船共還，建興復計，及弟道規、沛國劉毅、平昌孟昶、任城魏詠之、高平檀憑之、琅邪諸葛長人、太原王元德、隴西辛扈興、東莞童厚之，並同義謀。

translations.literal: Before long Xiu returned to Jingkou. The Emperor pleaded that an old wound had reopened and he could not keep pace on foot, and so he and Wuji returned together by boat. At Jianxing they renewed their plans, and together with his brother Daogui, Liu Yi of Pei, Meng Chang of Pingchang, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changren of Langya, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan, Xin Huxing of Longxi, and Tong Houzhi of Dongguan, they all shared one righteous conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiu returned to Jingkou. The Emperor pleaded that an old wound had reopened and he could not keep up on foot, and he and Wuji sailed back together. At Jianxing they renewed their plans with his brother Daogui, Liu Yi of Pei, Meng Chang of Pingchang, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changren of Langya, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan, Xin Huxing of Longxi, and Tong Houzhi of Dongguan. All joined in one righteous plot.

sentences.zh: 時桓修弟弘為青州刺史，鎮廣陵，道規為弘中兵參軍，昶為州主簿，乃令毅就昶謀共襲弘。

translations.literal: At the time Xuan's younger brother Hong was Governor of Qing Province and garrisoned Guangling. Daogui served as Army Headquarters Aide on Hong's staff, and Chang was chief clerk of the province. They therefore sent Yi to Chang to plan a joint surprise attack on Hong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuan's younger brother Hong was Governor of Qing Province, stationed at Guangling. Daogui served on Hong's staff as Army Headquarters Aide, and Chang was the provincial chief clerk. They sent Yi to Chang to plan a joint strike against Hong.

sentences.zh: 長人為豫州刺史刁逵左軍府參軍，謀據曆陽相應，元德、厚之謀於建鄴攻玄，克期齊發。

translations.literal: Changren was Left Army Headquarters Aide to Diao Kui, Governor of Yu Province, and planned to seize Liyang in support. Yuande and Houzhi plotted an attack on Xuan at Jianye. All fixed a date to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Changren served as Left Army Headquarters Aide to Diao Kui, Governor of Yu Province, and planned to seize Liyang in support. Yuande and Houzhi plotted to strike Xuan at Jianye. All fixed a day to rise together.

sentences.zh: 三年二月乙卯，帝托遊獵，與無忌、詠之、憑之，毅從弟藩，憑之從子韶、祗、隆、道濟，昶族弟懷玉等，集義徒凡二十七人，願從者百餘人。

translations.literal: On the day yimao in the second month of the third year, the Emperor pleaded a hunting excursion and gathered with Wuji, Yongzhi, Pingzhi, Yi's younger cousin Fan, Pingzhi's nephews Shao, Zhi, Long, and Daoji, Chang's younger clansman Huaiyu, and others. The righteous followers numbered twenty-seven in all, with more than a hundred willing to join them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao in the second month of the third year, the Emperor pleaded a hunting trip and gathered Wuji, Yongzhi, Pingzhi, Yi's younger cousin Fan, Pingzhi's nephews Shao, Zhi, Long, and Daoji, Chang's clansman Huaiyu, and others. The sworn company numbered twenty-seven, with more than a hundred men ready to follow.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，候城門開，無忌等義徒服傳詔服，稱詔居前，義眾馳入齊叫，吏士驚散，即斬修以徇。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen they waited for the city gates to open. Wuji and the other righteous followers wore imperial-messenger robes, proclaimed an edict, and went forward. The righteous masses galloped in shouting together. Officials and soldiers scattered in alarm. They at once beheaded Xiu and displayed his head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen they waited for the gates to open. Wuji and the others dressed as imperial messengers, proclaimed an edict, and led the charge. The righteous company galloped in with a great shout. Officials and soldiers fled in panic. Xiu was beheaded at once and his head displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之甚慟，厚加斂恤。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him with great grief and gave him generous burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept for him with deep grief and gave him generous burial honors.

sentences.zh: 昶勸弘其日出獵，未明，開門出獵人，昶、道規、毅等率壯士五六十人，因開門直入。

translations.literal: Chang urged Hong to go hunting that day. Before dawn, as the gate opened for the hunting party, Chang, Daogui, Yi, and others led fifty or sixty stalwart men and entered directly as the gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: Chang urged Hong to go hunting that day. Before dawn, when the gate opened for the hunt, Chang, Daogui, Yi, and others led fifty or sixty stalwart men straight through the gate.

sentences.zh: 弘方噉粥，即斬之，因收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Hong was just eating gruel when they beheaded him. They then gathered the troops and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was still eating his gruel when they cut him down. They then gathered the troops and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 義軍初克京城，修司馬刁弘率文武佐吏來赴，帝登城謂曰：「郭江州已奉乘輿反正于尋陽，我等並被密詔誅逆黨，今日賊玄之首已當梟於大航。

translations.literal: When the righteous army first took the capital, Xiu's Major Diao Hong led civil and military aides to come in support. The Emperor mounted the wall and said to them, "Governor Guo of Jiang Province has already received the imperial carriage and restored the rightful order at Xunyang. We too have all received secret edicts to execute the rebel faction. Today the head of the traitor Xuan should already be displayed at the Great Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army first took the capital, Xiu's Major Diao Hong led civil and military aides to come in support. The Emperor mounted the wall and called to them, "Governor Guo of Jiang Province has already received the imperial carriage and restored the rightful order at Xunyang. We too have received secret edicts to execute the rebel faction. By now the traitor Xuan's head should already hang at the Great Crossing.

sentences.zh: 諸君非大晉之臣乎？

translations.literal: Are you not ministers of great Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Surely you are still ministers of great Jin?

sentences.zh: 」弘等信之而退。

translations.literal: " Hong and the others believed him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong and his men took him at his word and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 毅既至，帝命誅弘等。

translations.literal: After Yi arrived, the Emperor ordered Hong and the others executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived, the Emperor ordered Hong and the others executed.

sentences.zh: 毅兄邁先在建鄴，事未發數日，帝遣同謀周安穆報之，使為內應。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Mai was already at Jianye. Several days before the affair broke out, the Emperor sent their fellow conspirator Zhou Anmu to report to him and make him an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Mai was already at Jianye. Several days before the plot broke, the Emperor sent their fellow conspirator Zhou Anmu to warn him and enlist him as an inside contact.

sentences.zh: 邁甚懼，安穆慮事發，馳歸。

translations.literal: Mai was greatly afraid. Anmu, fearing the affair would be exposed, galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Mai was terrified. Anmu, fearing exposure, galloped back.

sentences.zh: 時玄以邁為竟陵太守，邁便下船，欲之郡。

translations.literal: At the time Xuan had made Mai Administrator of Jingling, and Mai boarded a boat intending to go to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had just made Mai Administrator of Jingling, and Mai boarded a boat intending to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 是夜玄與邁書曰：「北府人情雲何？

translations.literal: That night Xuan wrote to Mai, "How stand the feelings of the Northern Headquarters men?
translations.idiomatic: That night Xuan wrote to Mai: "What is the mood among the Northern Headquarters men?

sentences.zh: 卿近見劉裕何所道？

translations.literal: What lately has Liu Yu said to you?
translations.idiomatic: What has Liu Yu lately said to you?

sentences.zh: 」邁謂玄已知其謀，晨起白之。

translations.literal: " Mai thought Xuan already knew of the plot. At dawn he went to report it.
translations.idiomatic: " Mai took this to mean Xuan already knew. At dawn he went to confess the plot.

sentences.zh: 玄驚，封邁為重安侯，又以不執安穆故殺之，誅元德、扈興、厚之等。

translations.literal: Xuan was alarmed. He enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an, but because Mai had not seized Anmu he also killed him, and executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was alarmed. He enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an, but because Mai had failed to seize Anmu he killed him as well, and executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and the others.

sentences.zh: 乃遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衛將軍皇甫敷北拒義軍。

translations.literal: He then sent Dunqiu Administrator Wu Fuzhi and Right Guard General Huangfu Fu north to resist the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched Dunqiu Administrator Wu Fuzhi and Right Guard General Huangfu Fu north to block the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝造遊擊將軍何澹之，左右見帝光曜滿室，以告澹之，澹之以白玄，玄不以為意，至是，聞義兵起，甚懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had visited General of Mobile Columns He Danzhi. His attendants saw his radiance filling the room and reported it to Danzhi. Danzhi told Xuan, but Xuan paid it no heed. Now, hearing that the righteous army had risen, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had visited General of Mobile Columns He Danzhi. His attendants saw his radiance fill the room and told Danzhi, who reported it to Xuan. Xuan paid no heed. Now, hearing that the righteous army had risen, he was deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「裕等甚弱，陛下何慮之深？

translations.literal: Someone said, "Yu and the others are very weak. Your Majesty, why do you fear them so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Yu and the others are very weak. Your Majesty, why fear them so deeply?

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「劉裕足為一世之雄，劉毅家無儋石之儲，摴蒱一擲百萬，何無忌，劉牢之之外甥，酷似其舅，共舉大事，何謂無成。

translations.literal: " Xuan said, "Liu Yu is fully the hero of an age. Liu Yi keeps not a single stone's store in his house, yet stakes a million at dice. He Wuji is Liu Laozhi's nephew by his sister and is the very image of his uncle. Together they undertake a great affair—how can it fail to succeed?
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "Liu Yu is a hero of the age. Liu Yi keeps not a stone's weight of grain in his house, yet stakes a million at dice. He Wuji is Liu Laozhi's nephew by his sister and is the very image of his uncle. Together they undertake a great affair—how can it fail?

sentences.zh: 」時眾推帝為盟主，以孟昶為長史，總後事，檀憑之為司馬，百姓願從者千餘人。

translations.literal: " At the time the masses pushed the Emperor as covenant leader. They made Meng Chang Chief Clerk to oversee rear affairs, Tan Pingzhi Major, and more than a thousand common people wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " The army then chose the Emperor as covenant leader, made Meng Chang Chief Clerk to manage rear affairs, Tan Pingzhi Major, and more than a thousand common people rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 軍次竹裏，移檄都下曰：

translations.literal: The army halted at Zhuli and issued a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Zhuli, it issued a proclamation to the capital that read:

sentences.zh: 夫成敗相因，理不常泰，狡焉肆虐，或遇聖明。

translations.literal: Success and failure follow one upon another; order is not eternally secure. When the cunning run wild, they sometimes meet a sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Success and failure follow one upon another; peace is never permanent. When the cunning run wild, they sometimes meet a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 自我大晉，屢遘陽九，隆安以來，皇家多故，貞良弊于豺狼，忠臣碎于虎口。

translations.literal: Since our great Jin repeatedly met with the calamities of the Yang Nine. From Long'an onward the royal house has suffered many troubles. The upright have been ruined by wolves, loyal ministers crushed in the tiger's maw.
translations.idiomatic: Since our great Jin has repeatedly met the calamities of the Yang Nine, the royal house has known one disaster after another from Long'an onward. The upright have been ruined by wolves, and loyal ministers crushed in the tiger's maw.

sentences.zh: 逆臣桓玄敢肆陵慢，阻兵荊郢，肆暴都邑，天未忘難，凶力實繁，踰年之間，遂傾皇祚。

translations.literal: The rebel minister Huan Xuan dared to act with insolent contempt, raised troops to block Jing and Ying, and wantonly ravaged the capital. Heaven had not yet forgotten our hardship, yet his wicked power was still great. Within little more than a year he overturned the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel minister Huan Xuan dared to act with insolent contempt, raised troops to hold Jing and Ying, and wantonly ravaged the capital. Heaven had not yet forgotten our hardship, yet his wicked power was still great. Within little more than a year he overturned the throne.

sentences.zh: 主上播越，流幸非所，神器沈辱，七廟毀墜，雖夏後之離浞、豷，有漢之遭莽、卓，方之於茲，未足為喻。

translations.literal: The sovereign was driven into exile and wandered where he should not. The sacred regalia sank into disgrace, the seven ancestral temples were cast down and destroyed. Though the flight of Xia after Han Zhuo and Yi, and the sufferings of Han under Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo, compared with this do not suffice as a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was driven into exile and wandered in places unfit for him. The sacred regalia sank into disgrace, and the seven ancestral temples were cast down. Even the flight of the Xia after Han Zhuo and Yi, and the sufferings of Han under Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo, scarcely serve as comparison.

sentences.zh: 自玄篡逆，於今曆載，彌年亢旱，人不聊生，士庶疲於轉輸，文武困於板築，室家分析，父子乖離，豈惟大東有杼軸之悲，摽梅有頃筐之怨而已哉！

translations.literal: Since Xuan's usurpation, years have already passed. Drought has lasted year after year. The people cannot live. Common folk are exhausted by transport levies, civil and military officials worn out by corvée labor. Families are split apart, fathers and sons separated—is this only the sorrow of the eastern lands over empty looms, or the longing of maidens over unfilled baskets?
translations.idiomatic: Since Xuan's usurpation years have passed. Drought has lingered year after year, and the people cannot live. Common folk are exhausted by transport levies; civil and military officials are worn out by forced labor. Families are split apart and fathers separated from sons. This is not merely the sorrow of empty looms in the east, or maidens' longing over unfilled baskets.

sentences.zh: 仰觀天文，俯察人事，此而可存，孰有可亡！

translations.literal: Looking up to observe the heavens, looking down to examine human affairs—if this can still endure, what could not be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the heavens and down to human affairs—if this can still endure, what could not be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 凡在有心，誰不扼腕。

translations.literal: All who have a heart—who does not wring his wrists in grief?
translations.idiomatic: Every man with a heart in his breast—who does not wring his wrists in grief?

sentences.zh: 裕等所以叩心泣血，不遑啟處者也。

translations.literal: This is why Yu and the others beat their breasts and weep blood, unable even to rest sitting or lying down.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Yu and the others beat their breasts and weep blood, finding no rest whether sitting or lying down.

sentences.zh: 是故夕寐宵興，搜獎忠烈，潛構崎嶇，過於履虎，乘機奮發，義不圖全。

translations.literal: Therefore we rise at night and sleep little, search out and reward the loyal and heroic, secretly build plans over rugged paths more perilous than treading on a tiger, seize the moment and strike fiercely, and in righteousness do not seek to preserve ourselves whole.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we rise at night and sleep little, search out and reward the loyal and heroic, secretly build plans over paths more perilous than treading on a tiger, seize the moment and strike fiercely, and in righteousness do not seek to save ourselves whole.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍劉毅、廣武將軍何無忌、鎮北主簿孟昶、兗州主簿魏詠之、甯遠將軍劉道規、龍驤參軍劉藩、振威將軍檀憑之等，忠烈斷金，精貫白日，荷戈俟奮，志在畢命。

translations.literal: Auxiliary State General Liu Yi, General of Broad Martial He Wuji, Chief Clerk to the Pacifying North Meng Chang, Chief Clerk of Yan Province Wei Yongzhi, General of Pacifying the Distance Liu Daogui, Dragon Cavalry Headquarters Aide Liu Fan, General Who Shakes Might Tan Pingzhi, and others—their loyalty cleaves metal, their spirit pierces the bright sun. Bearing weapons they await the moment to strike, resolved to give their lives to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary State General Liu Yi, General of Broad Martial He Wuji, Chief Clerk to the Pacifying North Meng Chang, Chief Clerk of Yan Province Wei Yongzhi, General of Pacifying the Distance Liu Daogui, Dragon Cavalry Headquarters Aide Liu Fan, General Who Shakes Might Tan Pingzhi, and others—their loyalty cleaves metal and their spirit pierces the bright sun. Bearing arms they await the moment to strike, resolved to give their lives to the end.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史毛璩，萬里齊契，掃定荊楚。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yi Province Mao Jin, though ten thousand li away, shares our covenant and will sweep and settle Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yi Province Mao Jin, though ten thousand li distant, stands in league with us and will sweep and settle Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史郭昶之奉迎主上，宮于尋陽。

translations.literal: Governor of Jiang Province Guo Yanzhi receives and escorts the sovereign, establishing his palace at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Jiang Province Guo Yanzhi receives and escorts the sovereign, establishing his residence at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮北參軍王元德等並率部曲，保據石頭。

translations.literal: Army Headquarters Aide Wang Yuande and others likewise lead their followers and hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Army Headquarters Aide Wang Yuande and others have likewise mustered their followers and hold Shitou.

sentences.zh: 揚武將軍諸葛長人收集義士，已據曆陽。

translations.literal: General Who Displays Martiality Zhuge Changren has gathered righteous warriors and already holds Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Displays Martiality Zhuge Changren has rallied righteous warriors and already holds Liyang.

sentences.zh: 征虜參軍庾賾之等潛相連結，以為內應。

translations.literal: Army Headquarters Aide Yu Yizhi and others secretly join in league and serve as inside contacts.
translations.idiomatic: Army Headquarters Aide Yu Yizhi and others have secretly joined the league and stand ready as inside contacts.

sentences.zh: 同力協契，所在蜂起，即日斬偽徐州刺史安成王修、青州刺史弘。

translations.literal: With united strength and shared covenant, they rose everywhere like swarming bees; that very day they beheaded the false Inspector of Xu Province, Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and Inspector of Qing Province Hong.
translations.idiomatic: With united strength and shared covenant they rose everywhere; that very day they beheaded the false Inspector of Xu Province, Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and Inspector of Qing Province Hong.

sentences.zh: 義眾既集，文武爭先，咸謂不有一統，則事無以輯。

translations.literal: Once the righteous masses had gathered, civil and military men vied to take the lead, all saying that without a single leader the affair could not be brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: Once the righteous army had gathered, civil and military men vied for the lead, all agreeing that without a single commander the cause could not be brought to order.

sentences.zh: 裕辭不獲命，遂總軍要，庶上憑祖宗之靈，下罄義夫之節，翦馘逋逆，蕩清京華。

translations.literal: Yu declined but could not refuse the mandate; he therefore assumed command of military affairs, hoping above to rely on the spirits of the ancestors and below to exhaust the integrity of righteous men, to cut down and behead fleeing rebels and sweep clean the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined but could not refuse; he therefore took command of the armies, trusting above in the spirits of the ancestors and below in the loyalty of righteous men, to cut down fleeing rebels and sweep clean the capital.

sentences.zh: 公侯諸君，或世樹忠貞，或身荷爵寵，而並俛眉猾豎，無由自效，顧瞻周道，寧不吊乎！

translations.literal: Lords and marquises—you who either for generations have planted loyalty and steadfastness, or yourselves have borne honors and favor—yet all bend your brows before this cunning upstart, with no way to offer your service. Looking back upon the way of Zhou, are you not to be mourned!
translations.idiomatic: Lords and marquises—you who for generations upheld loyalty or yourselves have borne honors and favor—yet all bow before this cunning upstart with no means to serve. When you look back upon the way of Zhou, is it not a cause for mourning?

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，良其會也。

translations.literal: Today's undertaking is truly the fitting moment.
translations.idiomatic: Today's undertaking is the moment that has awaited us.

sentences.zh: 裕以虛薄，才非古人，受任於既頹之運，接勢於已替之機，丹誠未宣，感慨憤激。

translations.literal: Yu, being hollow and thin in worth, his talent not that of men of old, received this charge in an already collapsing destiny and took up momentum at a time when the turn had already passed; his red sincerity yet unexpressed, he is stirred by feeling and inflamed with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, unworthy and lacking the talent of men of old, has taken this charge in a collapsing age and seized momentum when the turn had nearly passed. His loyal heart yet unspoken, he is moved and inflamed with indignation.

sentences.zh: 望霄漢以永懷，眄山川以增佇，投檄之日，神馳賊庭。

translations.literal: Gazing at the sky and the Milky Way in lasting remembrance, looking upon mountains and rivers to prolong his lingering—from the day the proclamation was sent forth, his spirit has raced to the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: He gazes toward heaven in lasting devotion and looks upon the land with growing resolve; from the day this proclamation went forth, his spirit has flown to the rebel court.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，遇吳甫之于江乘，帝躬執長刀，大呼，即斬甫之。

translations.literal: On the third month, wuwu day, he encountered Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng. The Emperor personally wielded a long blade, shouted loudly, and immediately beheaded Fuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the third month he encountered Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng. The Emperor personally seized a long blade, shouted, and at once cut Fuzhi down.

sentences.zh: 進至羅落橋，遇皇甫敷，檀憑之戰敗，死之，眾退，帝進戰彌厲，又斬敷首。

translations.literal: Advancing to Luoluo Bridge, he encountered Huangfu Fu. Tan Pingzhi was defeated in battle and killed; the army retreated. The Emperor pressed the fight all the more fiercely and again beheaded Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Luoluo Bridge, he met Huangfu Fu. Tan Pingzhi was defeated and killed, and the army fell back. The Emperor pressed the attack all the harder and again took Fu's head.

sentences.zh: 初，帝建大謀，有工相者相帝與無忌等近當大貴，惟云憑之無相。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor formed his great plot, there was a craftsman diviner who read the faces of the Emperor, Wuji, and the others and said they would soon attain great nobility, but declared that Pingzhi had no such countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor laid his great plan, a craftsman who read faces examined the Emperor, Wuji, and the others and said they would soon rise to great eminence, but declared that Pingzhi bore no such mark.

sentences.zh: 至是，憑之戰死，帝知其事必捷。

translations.literal: At this, Pingzhi died in battle, and the Emperor knew the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingzhi fell in battle, the Emperor knew the enterprise would surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 玄聞敷等沒，使桓謙屯東陵口，卞範之屯覆舟山西。

translations.literal: Xuan, hearing that Fu and the others had perished, sent Huan Qian to encamp at Dongling Kou and Bian Fanzhi to encamp west of Fuzhou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Fu and the others had fallen, Xuan sent Huan Qian to hold Dongling Kou and Bian Fanzhi to encamp west of Fuzhou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 己未，義軍進至覆舟東，張疑兵，以油帔冠諸樹，佈滿山谷。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day the righteous army advanced to the east of Fuzhou, deployed deceptive forces, placed oil-drenched cloaks atop the trees, and filled the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day the righteous army reached the east of Fuzhou, spread a screen of decoys, crowned the trees with oil-soaked cloaks, and filled the valleys with them.

sentences.zh: 帝先馳之，將士皆殊死戰，無不一當百，呼聲動天地。

translations.literal: The Emperor rode ahead at the forefront. Officers and soldiers all fought as if facing death; none failed to match one against a hundred. Their shouts shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor charged at the head. Officers and soldiers fought as if unto death, each man worth a hundred; their battle cries shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 因風縱火，煙焰張天，謙等大敗。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the wind they set fires ablaze; smoke and flame filled the sky. Qian and the others were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They sent fire with the wind; smoke and flame blotted out the sky. Qian and the others were routed.

sentences.zh: 玄始雖遣軍，而走意已決，別遣領軍殷仲文具舟石頭，聞謙敗，輕船南逸。

translations.literal: Though Xuan had at first sent out troops, his intent to flee was already fixed. Separately he dispatched Palace Attendant Yin Zhongwen to prepare boats at Shitou. Hearing of Qian's defeat, he fled south in light vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xuan had sent troops out, his mind was already set on flight. He had Palace Attendant Yin Zhongwen prepare boats at Shitou; when he heard of Qian's defeat, he slipped south in light craft.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝鎮石頭城，立留台百官，焚桓溫主于宣陽門外，造晉新主於太廟。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day the Emperor secured Shitou fortress, installed the officials of the rear capital, burned Huan Wen's ancestral tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and made new Jin ancestral tablets in the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the Emperor held Shitou fortress, established the rear-capital administration, burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and set up new Jin ancestral tablets in the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將追玄，命尚書王嘏率百官奉迎乘輿。

translations.literal: He dispatched generals to pursue Xuan and ordered Secretariat Director Wang Ga to lead the civil officials to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals in pursuit of Xuan and ordered Secretariat Director Wang Ga to lead the officials in welcoming the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 司徒王謐與眾議推帝領揚州，帝固辭，乃以謐為錄尚書事、領揚州刺史，帝為鎮軍將軍、都督八州諸軍事、徐州刺史、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Wang Mi discussed with the assembly and proposed that the Emperor take charge of Yang Province. The Emperor firmly declined. Thereupon Mi was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province; the Emperor was made General Who Pacifies the Army, Commander-in-Chief over all military affairs in eight provinces, Inspector of Xu Province, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Wang Mi consulted the assembly and urged the Emperor to take charge of Yang Province. The Emperor firmly refused. Mi was then made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province; the Emperor was made General Who Pacifies the Army, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in eight provinces, Inspector of Xu Province, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，晉陵人韋叟善相術，桓修令相帝當得州不，叟曰：「當得邊州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Sou of Jinyang was skilled in physiognomy. Huan Xiu had him read whether the Emperor would obtain a province. Sou said, "He will obtain an inspectorate of a frontier province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Sou of Jinyang was skilled in reading faces. Huan Xiu had him examine whether the Emperor would gain a provincial post. Sou said, "He will receive a frontier inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 」退而私於帝曰：「君相貴不可言。

translations.literal: " After withdrawing he spoke privately to the Emperor: "Your countenance's nobility cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: " After withdrawing he spoke privately to the Emperor: "Your noble bearing is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：」若中，當相用為司馬。

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed and said: "If you hit the mark, I shall employ you as Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor laughed and said, "If you prove right, I shall make you my marshal.

sentences.zh: 」至是，叟詣帝曰：「成王不負桐葉之信，公亦應不忘司馬之言。

translations.literal: " At this, Sou came to the Emperor and said: "King Cheng did not betray the pledge of the paulownia leaf; you likewise should not forget your word about the marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Sou came to the Emperor and said, "King Cheng did not break the pledge of the paulownia leaf; you too should not forget your promise about the marshal.

sentences.zh: 今不敢希鎮軍司馬，願得領軍佐。

translations.literal: Now I dare not hope for Marshal of the Pacifying Army, but wish to obtain an aide to the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not ask to be marshal to the Pacifying Army, but would be content with an aide's post under the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 」於是用焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was given the post.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛長人失期，為刁逵執送，未至而玄敗。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Changren had missed his deadline and was seized and sent under escort by Diao Kui. Before he arrived, Xuan was already defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changren had missed his rendezvous and was seized and sent under guard by Diao Kui, but before he arrived Xuan had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 玄經尋陽，江州刺史郭昶之為具乘輿法物。

translations.literal: Xuan passed through Xunyang; Inspector of Jiang Province Guo Changzhi prepared for him the imperial carriage and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan passed through Xunyang, where Inspector of Jiang Province Guo Changzhi furnished him with the imperial carriage and regalia.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州刺史王綏以江左冠族，又桓氏之甥，素甚陵帝，至是，及其父尚書左僕射愉有自疑志，並及誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Jing Province Wang Sui, being a leading clan of the Jiangzuo region and also a nephew of the Huan clan, had always greatly looked down upon the Emperor. At this time he, together with his father Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yu, nourished suspicions in their hearts, and both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jing Province Wang Sui, a leading house of the south and nephew of the Huan clan, had long treated the Emperor with contempt. Now he and his father, Left Vice Director Yu, both turned inward with suspicion and were executed.

sentences.zh: 四月戊子，奉武陵王遵為大將軍，承制，大赦，惟桓玄一祖後不免。

translations.literal: On the fourth month, wuzi day, they installed Prince of Wuling Zun as Grand General, acting by imperial commission, and proclaimed a general amnesty—all except the descendants of Huan Xuan's line.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the fourth month they installed Prince of Wuling Zun as Grand General with imperial commission, proclaimed a general amnesty, and exempted only the descendants of Huan Xuan's house.

sentences.zh: 桓玄之篡，王謐佐命，手解安帝璽紱。

translations.literal: At Huan Xuan's usurpation, Wang Mi assisted in the mandate and with his own hands removed Emperor An's seal cord.
translations.idiomatic: At Huan Xuan's usurpation Wang Mi had assisted the transfer of power and with his own hands removed Emperor An's seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，眾謂謐宜誅，惟帝素德謐，保持之。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, the masses said Mi ought to be executed, but the Emperor had always valued Mi's virtue and protected him.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, many said Mi deserved death, but the Emperor had long respected his character and kept him safe.

sentences.zh: 劉毅嘗因朝會，問謐璽紱所在，謐益懼。

translations.literal: Liu Yi once at a court assembly asked Mi where the seal cord was. Mi grew all the more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At a court assembly Liu Yi once asked Mi where the seal cord was kept. Mi grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 及王愉父子誅，謐從弟諶謂謐曰：「王駒無罪而誅，此是翦除勝己，兄既桓氏黨附，求免得乎？

translations.literal: When Wang Yu and his son were executed, Mi's younger male cousin from his clan Chen said to Mi: "Wang Ju was executed though guilty of nothing. This is cutting down those who surpass oneself. You, elder brother, were attached to the Huan faction—can you hope to escape unpunished?
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yu and his son were executed, Mi's clansman Chen said to him, "Wang Ju was killed though he had done no wrong. This is the clearing away of men who outshine their masters. You were tied to the Huan faction—do you think you can escape?

sentences.zh: 」駒，愉小字也。

translations.literal: " Ju was Yu's informal name.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju was Yu's informal name.

sentences.zh: 謐懼，奔曲阿。

translations.literal: Mi, in fear, fled to Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Mi fled to Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 帝箋白大將軍迎還，復其位。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote by memorial to the Grand General asking that he be brought back and his position restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor memorialized the Grand General asking that Mi be brought back and his office restored.

sentences.zh: 玄挾天子走江陵，又浮江東下，與劉毅、何無忌、劉道規等遇于崢嶸洲，眾軍大破之。

translations.literal: Xuan, leading the Son of Heaven with him, fled to Jiangling, then floated down the river eastward and met Liu Yi, He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and others at Zhengming Isle. The allied armies utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled with the Son of Heaven to Jiangling, then sailed downriver and met Liu Yi, He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and the others at Zhengming Isle. The allied armies broke him completely.

sentences.zh: 玄党殷仲文奉晉二皇后還建鄴。

translations.literal: Xuan's partisan Yin Zhongwen escorted the two Jin empresses back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's follower Yin Zhongwen escorted the two Jin empresses back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 玄復挾天子至江陵，因走南郡，太守王騰之、荊州別駕王康產奉天子入南郡府。

translations.literal: Xuan again led the Son of Heaven to Jiangling, then fled to Nan Commandery. Administrator Wang Tengzhi and Jing Province Registrar Wang Kangchan received the Son of Heaven into the Nan Commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan again brought the Son of Heaven to Jiangling, then fled toward Nan Commandery. Administrator Wang Tengzhi and Jing Province Registrar Wang Kangchan received the Son of Heaven into the Nan Commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 初，益州刺史毛璩遣從孫佑之與參軍費恬送弟喪下州，璩弟子修之時為玄屯騎校尉，誘玄入蜀，至枚回洲，恬與佑之迎射之，益州督護馮遷斬玄，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Yi Province Mao Jin had sent his grandnephew Youzhi, together with staff officer Fei Tian, to escort his younger brother's funeral downriver. Jin's nephew Xiuzhi was then Cavalry Commandant in Xuan's service and lured Xuan into Shu. At Meihui Isle, Tian and Youzhi met him with arrows; Yi Province Supervising Officer Feng Qian beheaded Xuan and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Inspector of Yi Province Mao Jin had sent his grandnephew Youzhi and staff officer Fei Tian to escort his brother's funeral downriver. Jin's nephew Xiuzhi, then Cavalry Commandant under Xuan, lured Xuan toward Shu. At Meihui Isle Tian and Youzhi ambushed him with arrows; Yi Province Supervising Officer Feng Qian cut off Xuan's head and sent it to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 玄從子振逃于華容之湧中，招集逆黨，襲江陵城，騰之、康產皆被殺。

translations.literal: Xuan's nephew Zhen fled into the marshes of Huarong, gathered rebel partisans, and stormed Jiangling city. Tengzhi and Kangchan were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's nephew Zhen hid in the marshes of Huarong, rallied rebel bands, and stormed Jiangling. Tengzhi and Kangchan were both killed.

sentences.zh: 桓謙先匿沮川，亦聚眾應振。

translations.literal: Huan Qian, who had first hidden at Juchuan, also gathered troops and responded to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian, who had first taken refuge at Juchuan, also raised forces and joined Zhen.

sentences.zh: 為玄舉哀，立喪庭。

translations.literal: They performed mourning rites for Xuan and set up a mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: They mourned Xuan and erected a mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 謙率眾官奉璽綬于安帝。

translations.literal: Qian led the officials in presenting the seal cord to Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Qian led the officials in restoring the seal and cord to Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 劉毅、何無忌進及桓振戰，敗績於靈溪。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and He Wuji advanced and fought Zhen, but were defeated at Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi and He Wuji pressed forward against Zhen and were defeated at Lingxi.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝領青州刺史，甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor took charge as Inspector of Qing Province, with a hundred armored men entering the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor assumed the post of Inspector of Qing Province and entered the palace hall with a hundred armored guards.

sentences.zh: 盧循浮海破廣州，獲刺史吳隱之，即以循為廣州刺史，以其党徐道覆為始興相。

translations.literal: Lu Xun crossed the sea by boat, captured Guangzhou, and took Governor Wu Yinshi prisoner. He then installed Xun as Inspector of Guang Province and his partisan Xu Daofu as Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sailed across the sea, took Guangzhou, and captured Governor Wu Yinshi. He made Xun Inspector of Guang Province and appointed his follower Xu Daofu Administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，進帝督交、廣二州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year the Emperor was promoted to command Jiao and Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year the Emperor was given command over Jiao and Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 十月，論匡復勳，封帝豫章郡公，邑萬戶，賜絹三萬疋。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, in reckoning merit for restoring the dynasty, the Emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang with a fief of ten thousand households and granted thirty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, for merit in restoring the dynasty, the Emperor was enfeoffed Duke of Yuzhang with a fief of ten thousand households and granted thirty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其餘封賞各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining enfeoffments and rewards were graded according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: The other enfeoffments and rewards were apportioned by rank of service.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，司徒、錄尚書、揚州刺史王謐薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year, Minister over the Masses, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yang Province Wang Mi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year Wang Mi, Minister over the Masses, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yang Province, died.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，征帝入輔，授侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書事，徐、兗二州刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Emperor was summoned to assist at court and appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yang Province, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, while retaining his posts as Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Emperor was called to court and appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yang Province, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, while retaining his posts in Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 表解兗州。

translations.literal: He memorialized to relinquish Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝遣冠軍劉敬宣伐蜀賊譙縱，無功而還。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had dispatched Champion General Liu Jingxuan to attack the Shu rebel Qiao Zong, but he returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had sent Champion General Liu Jingxuan against the Shu rebel Qiao Zong, but Jingxuan returned without victory.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝以敬宣挫退，遜位，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Jingxuan had been driven back, the Emperor offered to yield his office, but the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, blaming himself for Jingxuan's setback, the Emperor offered to step down, but the court would not accept.

sentences.zh: 十月，乃降為中軍將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was demoted to General of the Center, while his commission to open an headquarters remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was reduced to General of the Center, though his headquarters commission remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，偽燕主慕容超大掠淮北。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year the false Yan ruler Murong Chao raided heavily north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year the Yan pretender Murong Chao launched a major raid north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝抗表北討，以丹陽尹孟昶監中軍留府事。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor submitted a memorial to campaign north and appointed Chief of Jinyang Meng Chang overseer of central headquarters affairs left behind at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor memorialized to campaign north and left Chief of Jinyang Meng Chang to oversee headquarters affairs at the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃浮淮入泗，五月，至下邳，留船，步軍進琅邪，所過築城留守。

translations.literal: He then sailed the Huai into the Si, and in the fifth month reached Xiapi, left the boats there, and marched overland into Langya, building fortified posts and garrisons wherever he passed.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed up the Huai into the Si and, in the fifth month, reached Xiapi. Leaving the boats behind, he marched overland into Langya, building fortified posts and leaving garrisons at every stage.

sentences.zh: 超大將公孫五樓請斷大峴，堅壁清野以待，超不從。

translations.literal: Chao's great general Gongsun Wulou urged that the Great Pass be blocked and a scorched-earth defense mounted to await the enemy, but Chao would not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's chief general Gongsun Wulou urged him to hold the Great Pass, fortify the walls, and strip the countryside bare while waiting, but Chao refused.

sentences.zh: 初謀是役，議者以為賊若嚴守大峴，軍無所資，何能自反？

translations.literal: At the first planning of this campaign, those in council said that if the enemy strictly held the Great Pass the army would have no supplies—how could it turn back on its own?
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign was first debated, critics said that if the enemy held the Great Pass the army would run out of supplies and have no way to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑性貪，略不及遠，既幸其勝，且愛其穀，必將引我，且亦輕戰。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy by nature; in plunder they do not look far ahead. Once they have tasted victory and grown fond of the grain here, they are sure to draw us on, and they will also fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei are greedy by nature and plunder without looking far ahead. Once they taste victory and covet the grain here, they will surely draw us on—and they will fight rashly besides.

sentences.zh: 師一入峴，吾何患焉。

translations.literal: Once the army enters the pass, what have I to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Once our army is through the pass, what have I to fear?

sentences.zh: 」及入峴，帝舉手指天曰：「吾事濟矣。

translations.literal: " When they entered the pass, the Emperor raised his hand and pointed to heaven, saying: "My affair is assured.
translations.idiomatic: " When they entered the pass the Emperor lifted his hand toward heaven and said, "The matter is settled.

sentences.zh: 」眾問其故，帝曰：「師既過險，士有必死之志，餘糧棲畝，軍無匱乏之憂，勝可必矣。」

translations.literal: " The troops asked the reason. The Emperor said: "The army has already passed the peril; the soldiers have the will to die. Grain remains standing in the fields, and the army has no worry of shortage. Victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: " The troops asked why. The Emperor said, "We have passed the danger; every man is ready to die. Grain still stands in the fields, and the army need not fear want. Victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 六月，超留羸老守廣固，使其廣甯王賀刺盧及公孫五樓悉力據臨朐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chao left the weak and aged to hold Guanggu and sent his Prince of Guangning He Cilu together with Gongsun Wulou to hold Linqu with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chao left the weak and aged to defend Guanggu and sent Prince of Guangning He Cilu and Gongsun Wulou to hold Linqu with their full strength.

sentences.zh: 去城四十里有巨蔑水，超告五樓急據之。

translations.literal: Forty li from the city was the Jumei River. Chao told Wulou to seize it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li from the city lay the Jumei River. Chao ordered Wulou to seize it immediately.

sentences.zh: 比至，為龍驤將軍孟龍符所保，五樓乃退。

translations.literal: By the time Wulou arrived, Dragon Cavalry General Meng Longfu had already seized it, and Wulou withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wulou could reach it, Dragon Cavalry General Meng Longfu had already taken the crossing, and Wulou fell back.

sentences.zh: 大軍分車四千兩為二翼，方軌徐行，車張幰，禦者執肖，以騎為遊軍，軍令嚴肅。

translations.literal: The great army divided four thousand chariots into two wings and advanced in measured formation, chariots hung with curtains while the drivers held leather shields; cavalry served as roaming detachments, and military discipline was strict.
translations.idiomatic: The main army split four thousand chariots into two wings and advanced in close formation, curtains drawn on the chariots and drivers holding leather shields, with cavalry as roaming screens. Discipline was severe.

sentences.zh: 比及臨朐，賊騎交至，帝命兗州刺史劉藩、并州刺史劉道憐等陷其陣。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Linqu, enemy cavalry came repeatedly to the attack. The Emperor ordered Inspector of Yan Province Liu Fan, Inspector of Bing Province Liu Daolin, and others to break their formations.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Linqu enemy horsemen attacked again and again. The Emperor ordered Inspector of Yan Province Liu Fan, Inspector of Bing Province Liu Daolin, and others to smash their lines.

sentences.zh: 日向昃，戰猶酣，帝用參軍胡藩策，襲克臨朐，賊乃大奔。

translations.literal: When the sun had passed the zenith the fighting was still fierce. The Emperor adopted the plan of staff officer Hu Fan, struck and captured Linqu, and the enemy fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The sun was already westering and the battle still raged. The Emperor took staff officer Hu Fan's advice, stormed Linqu, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 超遁還廣固，獲其玉璽、豹尾、輦等，送於都。

translations.literal: Chao fled back to Guanggu. They captured his jade seal, leopard-tail banners, imperial carriage, and the like, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled back to Guanggu. The army captured his jade seal, leopard-tail standards, imperial carriage, and the like, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙子，克廣固大城，超固其小城。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day they captured the outer city of Guanggu; Chao held fast in the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day they took the outer city of Guanggu; Chao shut himself in the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 乃設長圍以守之，館谷於青土，停江、淮轉輸。

translations.literal: They then set a long encirclement to hold him there, quartered the army on the grain of Qing province, and suspended transport from the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: They then drew a long siege around him, fed the army from Qing province's grain, and halted shipments from the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 七月，超尚書郎張綱乞師于姚興，自長安反，泰山太守申宣執送之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Chao's Master of Writing Lang Zhang Gang went to ask Yao Xing for troops, returned from Chang'an, and was seized and sent under guard by Administrator of Taishan Shen Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chao's Master of Writing Lang Zhang Gang went to Yao Xing to ask for troops, returned from Chang'an, and was seized and sent under guard by Taishan Administrator Shen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 綱有巧思，先是，帝修攻具，城上人曰：「汝不得張綱，何能為也。

translations.literal: Gang was ingenious in design. Earlier, while the Emperor was building siege engines, the men on the walls said: "Without Zhang Gang, what can you do?
translations.idiomatic: Gang was a clever inventor. While the Emperor was building siege engines, the men on the walls had said, "Without Zhang Gang, what can you accomplish?

sentences.zh: 」及至，升諸樓車以示之，城內莫不失色。

translations.literal: " When Gang arrived, they raised him on a tower chariot to show him to the city. Inside the walls none failed to lose color.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gang arrived they lifted him onto a tower chariot to display him to the city. Inside the walls every face went pale.

sentences.zh: 超既求救不獲，綱反見虜，乃求稱藩，割大峴為界，獻馬千匹，不聽。

translations.literal: Chao, having failed to obtain relief and now seeing Gang taken captive, then asked to submit as a vassal, cede the Great Pass as a boundary, and present a thousand horses, but the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Relief did not come, and Gang was now a captive. Chao then offered to submit as a vassal, cede the Great Pass as a border, and present a thousand horses, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時姚興遣使，聲言將涉淮左，帝謂曰：「爾報姚興，我定青州，將過函谷，虜能自送，今其時矣。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Xing sent an envoy declaring that he would cross the left bank of the Huai. The Emperor told him: "Go tell Yao Xing: once I settle Qing Province I shall pass through Hangu Pass. If the barbarians wish to deliver themselves up, the time is now.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing then sent an envoy declaring that he would cross the Huai. The Emperor told him, "Go tell Yao Xing: when I have settled Qing Province I shall march through Hangu Pass. If the barbarians mean to surrender themselves, the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 」錄事參軍劉穆之遽入曰：「此言不足威敵，容能怒彼。

translations.literal: " Recording Officer staff member Liu Muzhi hurried in and said: "These words are not enough to overawe the enemy and may only enrage him.
translations.idiomatic: " Recording Officer Liu Muzhi hurried in and said, "Those words will not frighten the enemy—they may only provoke him.

sentences.zh: 若鮮卑未拔，西羌又至，公何以待之？

translations.literal: If the Xianbei are not yet taken and the Western Qiang arrive as well, how will you meet them?
translations.idiomatic: If the Xianbei are not yet broken and the Western Qiang come too, how will you face them?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃笑曰：「此兵機也，非子所及。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then laughed and said: "This is military stratagem—not something you can grasp.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor laughed and said, "That is military stratagem—not a matter within your reach.

sentences.zh: 羌若能救，不有先聲，是自強也。」

translations.literal: If the Qiang could save them, they would not need a prior declaration; making one is only to strengthen ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: If the Qiang could save them they would not need a warning first; giving one only steels our own ranks."

sentences.zh: 十月，張綱修攻具成，設飛樓縣梯，木幔板屋，冠以牛皮，弓矢無所用之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zhang Gang finished the siege engines: flying towers with suspended ladders, wooden screens and plank shelters roofed with oxhide, against which bow and arrow were useless.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Gang completed the siege engines—flying towers with hanging ladders, wooden screens and plank shelters roofed in oxhide, proof against bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 劉毅遣上党太守趙恢以千餘人來援，帝夜潛遣軍會之。

translations.literal: Liu Yi sent Shangdang Administrator Zhao Hui with more than a thousand men as reinforcements. The Emperor secretly dispatched troops by night to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi sent Shangdang Administrator Zhao Hui with more than a thousand men as reinforcements. The Emperor secretly moved troops by night to meet them.

sentences.zh: 明旦，恢眾五千，方道而進，每晉使將到，輒復如之。

translations.literal: At dawn Hui's force numbered five thousand and advanced in formation on the road; whenever Jin envoys were about to arrive, they repeated the maneuver.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Hui's force had swelled to five thousand and marched in formation along the road; each time a Jin envoy was due to arrive they staged the display again.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁亥，屠廣固，超踰城走，追獲之，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: On the second month, dinghai day, of the sixth year they sacked Guanggu. Chao fled over the wall but was pursued and captured, then executed in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the second month in the sixth year they sacked Guanggu. Chao fled over the wall, was pursued and captured, and was executed in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 殺其王公以下，納生口萬餘，馬二千匹。

translations.literal: They killed his princes and officials and below, took more than ten thousand captives, and two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: They killed his princes, officials, and their followers, took more than ten thousand captives, and seized two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 初，帝之北也，徐道覆勸盧循乘虛而出，循不從，道覆乃至番禺說循曰：「今日之機，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor marched north, Xu Daofu urged Lu Xun to strike while the capital lay open, but Xun would not follow. Daofu then went to Panyu and said to Xun: "Today's opportunity must on no account be lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched north, Xu Daofu urged Lu Xun to strike while the capital lay open, but Xun refused. Daofu then went to Panyu and told him, "Today's opportunity must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 若克京都，劉公雖還，無能為也。

translations.literal: If we take the capital, even should Liu return he will be unable to act.
translations.idiomatic: If we seize the capital, Liu Yu may return, but he will be powerless.

sentences.zh: 」循從之。

translations.literal: " Xun followed the advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun agreed.

sentences.zh: 是月，寇南康、廬陵、豫章諸郡，郡守皆奔走。

translations.literal: That month they raided the commanderies of Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; the administrators all fled.
translations.idiomatic: That month they raided Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; every administrator fled.

sentences.zh: 時帝將鎮下邳，進兵河、洛，及征使至，即日班師。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was about to garrison Xiapi and advance on the Yellow River and Luoyang, but when the imperial dispatch arrived he turned the army back that very day.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was preparing to garrison Xiapi and advance toward the Yellow River and Luoyang, but when the imperial dispatch arrived he marched back the same day.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍何無忌與道覆戰，敗死于豫章，內外震駭，朝議欲奉乘輿北走。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South He Wuji fought Daofu and was defeated and killed at Yuzhang. Within and without the court were shaken; at court they debated escorting the imperial carriage north.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the South He Wuji fought Daofu, was defeated, and died at Yuzhang. Court and country were shaken, and some at court urged moving the imperial carriage north.

sentences.zh: 帝次山陽，聞敗，卷甲與數十人造江上征問，知賊尚未至。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at Shanyang. Hearing of the defeat, he rolled up his armor and with several dozen men went to the river to inquire of the campaign, and learned that the rebels had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor halted at Shanyang. Hearing of the defeat, he forced-marched with a few dozen men to the river to gather news and learned that the rebels had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 四月癸未，帝至都。

translations.literal: On the fourth month, guiwei day, the Emperor reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the fourth month the Emperor reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉毅自表南征，帝以賊新捷鋒銳，須嚴軍偕進，使劉藩止之，毅不從。

translations.literal: Liu Yi memorialized to campaign south himself. The Emperor, judging the rebels fresh from victory and sharp in the attack, said a strict combined advance was needed and sent Liu Fan to stop him, but Yi would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi volunteered to campaign south in person. The Emperor, judging the rebels fresh from victory and still keen, said they must advance in strength together and sent Liu Fan to hold Yi back, but Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 五月壬午，盧循敗毅于桑落洲。

translations.literal: On the fifth month, renwu day, Lu Xun defeated Yi at Sangluo Isle.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the fifth month Lu Xun defeated Yi at Sangluo Isle.

sentences.zh: 及審帝凱入，相視失色，欲還尋陽，平江陵，據二州以抗朝廷。

translations.literal: When they learned the Emperor had entered in triumph, they looked at one another and lost color, wishing to return to Xunyang, pacify Jiangling, and hold the two provinces to resist the court.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned the Emperor had entered the capital in triumph, they looked at one another and went pale, intending to fall back to Xunyang, secure Jiangling, and hold the two provinces against the court.

sentences.zh: 道覆請乘勝遂下，爭之旬日，乃從。

translations.literal: Daofu urged pressing the advantage and advancing downstream; after ten days of dispute, Xun at last agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu urged that they press their victory and push downstream; after ten days of argument Xun finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 于時北師始還，傷痍未復，戰士才數千，賊眾十餘萬，舳艫亙千里。

translations.literal: At that time the northern army had just returned, wounds were not yet healed, the soldiers numbered only a few thousand, the rebels more than a hundred thousand, and their ships stretched a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army had just returned, its wounds still unhealed. The soldiers numbered only a few thousand against more than a hundred thousand rebels, their fleet stretching a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 孟昶、諸葛長人懼，欲擁天子過江，帝曰：「今兵士雖少，猶足一戰，若其克濟，臣主同休；

translations.literal: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changren were afraid and wished to escort the Son of Heaven across the river. The Emperor said: "Our soldiers are few today, yet still enough for one battle. If we succeed, lord and subject share the triumph;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changren were terrified and wanted to escort the Son of Heaven across the river. The Emperor said, "Our soldiers are few, but enough for one fight. If we prevail, lord and subject share the victory;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，不復能草間求活，吾計決矣。

translations.literal: if not, we can no longer seek life hiding in the grass. My plan is decided."
translations.idiomatic: if not, we can no longer scrape out a living in the weeds. My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 」初，帝征慕容超，惟孟昶勸行，丙辰，昶乃表天子，引罪，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor campaigned against Murong Chao, only Meng Chang had urged the expedition. On the bingchen day Chang memorialized the Son of Heaven accepting blame and took poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor had campaigned against Murong Chao, Meng Chang alone had urged him to go. On the bingchen day Chang memorialized the throne accepting blame and died by poison.

sentences.zh: 時議者欲分兵屯守諸津，帝曰：「賊眾我寡，分其兵則人測虛實，一處失利，則沮三軍之心，若聚眾石頭，則眾力不分。

translations.literal: At the time those in council wished to divide the army and garrison the various fords. The Emperor said: "The rebels are many and we are few. If we divide our forces, men will measure our strength and weakness. One place lost will break the heart of the whole army. If we gather at Shitou, our strength will not be divided.
