translations.idiomatic: Councilors then urged dividing the army to hold the river crossings. The Emperor said, "The enemy outnumbers us. Split our forces and they will read our weakness; lose one post and the whole army loses heart. Gather at Shitou and our strength stays whole.

sentences.zh: 」戊午，帝移鎮石城。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day the Emperor moved his headquarters to Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day the Emperor shifted his headquarters to Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，賊大至，帝曰：「賊若新亭直上，且將避之；

translations.literal: On the yichou day the rebels arrived in force. The Emperor said: "If the rebels come straight up from Xinting, we shall for the moment give way;
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day the rebels came in force. The Emperor said, "If they drive straight up from Xinting, we will pull back for now;

sentences.zh: 若回泊蔡洲，成禽耳。

translations.literal: if they turn and anchor at Caizhou, they are as good as captured."
translations.idiomatic: if they turn and moor at Caizhou, they are as good as ours."

sentences.zh: 」徐道覆欲自新亭焚舟而戰，循多疑少決，每求萬全，乃泊蔡洲以待軍潰。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu wished to burn the boats at Xinting and fight, but Xun was suspicious and slow to decide, always seeking complete safety, and so anchored at Caizhou to wait for the army to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu wanted to burn the boats at Xinting and give battle, but Xun was suspicious and indecisive, always insisting on perfect safety, and moored at Caizhou to wait for the army to fall apart.

sentences.zh: 帝登石頭以望，見之，悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended Shitou to look out and, seeing this, was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor climbed Shitou to look out, saw what had happened, and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賊設伏于南岸，疑兵向白石。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day the rebels set an ambush on the south bank and sent a screen of decoys toward Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day the rebels laid an ambush on the south bank and sent a feint toward Baishi.

sentences.zh: 帝率劉毅、諸葛長人北拒焉，留參軍徐赤特戍查浦，戒令勿戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor led Liu Yi and Zhuge Changren north to meet them, leaving staff officer Xu Chite to garrison Chabu with orders not to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led Liu Yi and Zhuge Changren north to meet them, leaving staff officer Xu Chite to hold Chabu under strict orders not to engage.

sentences.zh: 帝既北，賊焚查浦而至張侯橋，赤特與戰，大敗，賊進屯丹陽郡。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor had gone north, the rebels burned Chabu and reached Zhanghou Bridge. Chite gave battle and was utterly defeated; the rebels advanced and encamped in Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor marched north, the rebels burned Chabu and pushed to Zhanghou Bridge. Chite gave battle and was routed; the rebels advanced and encamped in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝馳還石頭，斬徐赤特。

translations.literal: The Emperor galloped back to Shitou and executed Xu Chite.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor raced back to Shitou and executed Xu Chite.

sentences.zh: 解甲久之，乃出陣于南塘。

translations.literal: After the troops had rested out of armor for a long while, he then deployed his formation at Nantang.
translations.idiomatic: After the men had rested out of armor for some time, he deployed his line at Nantang.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申，循自蔡洲退，將還歸尋陽，帝遣輔國將軍王仲德等追之。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the seventh month Xun withdrew from Caizhou, intending to return to Xunyang. The Emperor sent General Who Assists the State Wang Zhongde and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the seventh month Xun pulled back from Caizhou, intending to return to Xunyang. The Emperor sent General Who Assists the State Wang Zhongde and others after him.

sentences.zh: 使建威將軍孫處自海道襲番禺，戒之曰：「我十二月必破祅寇，卿亦足至番禺，先傾其巢窟也。」

translations.literal: He sent General Who Establishes Might Sun Chu by the sea route to strike Panyu and warned him: "I shall surely break the demonic rebels by the twelfth month. You too can reach Panyu in time—first overturn their nest."
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Who Establishes Might Sun Chu by sea to strike Panyu and told him, "I will break these rebels by the twelfth month. You can reach Panyu in time—strike their nest first."

sentences.zh: 十月，帝率舟師南伐，使劉毅監太尉留府。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor led the fleet south in campaign and left Liu Yi to oversee the headquarters left behind at the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor led the fleet south and left Liu Yi to oversee affairs at the capital headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是月，徐道覆寇江陵，荊州刺史劉道規大破之，道覆走還湓口。

translations.literal: That month Xu Daofu raided Jiangling, but Inspector of Jing Province Liu Daogui utterly defeated him and Daofu fled back to Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xu Daofu attacked Jiangling, but Inspector of Jing Province Liu Daogui routed him and Daofu fled back to Penkou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，孫處至番禺，克其城，盧循父嘏奔始興，處撫其人以守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Sun Chu reached Panyu and captured the city. Lu Xun's father Gu fled to Shixing, and Chu comforted the people and garrisoned the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sun Chu reached Panyu and took the city. Lu Xun's father Gu fled to Shixing, and Chu reassured the people and held the town.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯，大軍次大雷。

translations.literal: On the jimao day of the twelfth month the great army halted at Dalei.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the twelfth month the main army halted at Dalei.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賊方江而下，帝躬提幡鼓，命眾軍齊力擊之，軍中多萬鈞神弩，所至莫不摧陷。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day the rebels came down the river. The Emperor personally took up banner and drum and ordered all the armies to strike together. The army had many divine crossbows of ten-thousand-jun draw, and wherever they reached nothing failed to be shattered.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day the rebels came downriver. The Emperor himself took up banner and drum and ordered a united attack. The army fielded many ten-thousand-jun crossbows, and nothing they struck remained standing.

sentences.zh: 帝自于中流蹙之，因風水之勢，賊艦悉薄西岸，岸上軍先備火具焚之，大敗。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself pressed them from midstream. Using the force of wind and water, the rebel ships were all driven to the west bank. The troops on shore, having prepared fire gear beforehand, burned them, and the rebels were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself pressed them from midstream. Wind and current drove the rebel ships against the west bank, where the shore troops, fire gear ready, burned them. The enemy was broken completely.

sentences.zh: 循還尋陽，遂走豫章，悉力柵左裏。

translations.literal: Xun returned to Xunyang, then fled to Yuzhang and used all his strength to fortify Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fell back to Xunyang, then fled to Yuzhang and threw all his strength into fortifying Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 丙申，大軍次左裏，將戰，帝麾之，麾竿折，幡沈于水，眾咸懼，帝笑曰：「昔覆舟之役亦如此，今勝必矣。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day the great army halted at Zuoli. As battle was about to begin, the Emperor waved his command baton; the shaft broke and the banner sank in the water. All were afraid. The Emperor laughed and said: "At the battle of Fuzhou it was also thus. Victory is certain now.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day the main army halted at Zuoli. As battle was about to begin the Emperor raised his command baton; the shaft snapped and the banner sank in the water. All were afraid. The Emperor laughed and said, "It was just like this at Fuzhou. Victory is certain now.

sentences.zh: 」攻其柵，循單舸走，眾皆降。

translations.literal: " They attacked the fort. Xun fled alone in a small boat, and the masses all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " They stormed the fort. Xun escaped alone in a small boat, and his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師旋，晉帝遣侍中黃門勞師於行所。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Jin Emperor sent a Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate officer to honor the troops where they halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the Jin Emperor sent a Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate officer to honor the troops on the march.

sentences.zh: 七年正月己未，振旅而歸，改授大將軍、揚州牧，給班劍二十人，本官並如故。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day of the first month of the seventh year he returned with his troops refreshed and was reassigned Grand General and Governor of Yang Province, granted twenty ceremonial swords, while his original posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the first month in the seventh year he returned with his army refreshed and was reassigned Grand General and Governor of Yang Province with twenty ceremonial swords, while retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 凡南北征伐戰亡者，並列上賻贈，屍喪未反者，遣主帥迎接，致還本土。

translations.literal: All who had died in the northern and southern campaigns were listed for funeral gifts. Where bodies had not been returned, commanders were sent to receive them and restore them to their native lands.
translations.idiomatic: All who had fallen in the northern and southern campaigns were listed for burial gifts. Where bodies had not come home, commanders were sent to receive them and return them to their native lands.

sentences.zh: 二月，盧循至番禺，為孫處所破，收余眾南走。

translations.literal: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu, was defeated by Sun Chu, gathered his remnant forces, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu, was broken by Sun Chu, gathered his remnant forces, and fled south.

sentences.zh: 劉藩、孟懷玉斬徐道覆於始興。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu cut off Xu Daofu at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 自晉中興以來，朝綱弛紊，權門兼併，百姓流離，不得保其產業。

translations.literal: Since the restoration of Jin, court discipline had grown lax, powerful families had swallowed up holdings, and the people had been driven from place to place, unable to keep their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin's restoration court discipline had slackened, powerful families had swallowed up holdings, and common people had been driven from their homes, unable to keep their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 桓玄頗欲厘改，竟不能行。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan had wished somewhat to reform this, but in the end could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had wanted to reform this, but in the end could not enforce it.

sentences.zh: 帝既作輔，大示軌則，豪強肅然，遠近禁止。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor became regent he set the standards plainly. The powerful families grew sober, and lawlessness was forbidden near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor became regent he made the standards plain. Powerful families fell silent, and lawlessness was forbidden far and near.

sentences.zh: 至是，會稽余姚虞亮復藏匿亡命千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again concealed more than a thousand fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again sheltered more than a thousand fugitives.

sentences.zh: 帝誅亮，免會稽內史司馬休之。

translations.literal: The Emperor executed Liang and dismissed Interior Secretary Sima Xiuzhi of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor executed Liang and removed Sima Xiuzhi from his post as Interior Secretary of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 晉帝又申前詔，帝固辭。

translations.literal: The Jin Emperor again repeated the earlier decree, but the Emperor firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Emperor again repeated the earlier decree, but the Emperor firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 於是改授太尉、中書監，乃受命，奉送黃鉞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat. He then accepted the mandate and was presented with the yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat, accepted the mandate, and was presented with the yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜惠度斬盧循父子，函七首送都。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiao Province Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and his son and sent their heads in a box to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiao Province Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and his son and sent their heads to the capital in a box.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸州郡所遣秀才、孝廉多非其人，帝乃表申明舊例，策試之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the presented scholars and filial-and-incorrupt candidates sent up by the provinces and commanderies had often been unworthy men. The Emperor therefore memorialized to clarify the old rules and tested them by examination.
translations.idiomatic: The presented scholars and filial-and-incorrupt candidates sent up from the provinces had often been unworthy. The Emperor memorialized to restore the old rules and tested them by examination.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史劉道規疾患，求歸，八年四月，改授豫州刺史，以豫州刺史劉毅代之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Liu Daogui fell ill and asked to retire. In the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned Inspector of Yu Province, and Liu Yi, Inspector of Yu Province, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jing Province Liu Daogui fell ill and asked to retire. In the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned to Yu Province, and Liu Yi of Yu Province replaced him.

sentences.zh: 毅既有雄才大志，與帝俱興復晉室，自謂京城、廣陵功足相抗，雖權事推帝，而心不服也。

translations.literal: Yi had heroic talent and great ambition. He and the Emperor had together restored the Jin house, and he considered his achievements at the capital and at Guangling equal to the Emperor's. Though in outward affairs he deferred to the Emperor, in his heart he did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had heroic talent and great ambition. He and the Emperor had restored Jin together, and he considered his achievements at the capital and at Guangling a match for the Emperor's. Outwardly he deferred to him, but in his heart he did not submit.

sentences.zh: 厚自矜許，朝士素望者並多歸之，與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施並深相結。

translations.literal: He praised himself lavishly, and many court officials of long-standing reputation joined him. He formed deep ties with Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xie Hun and Chief of Jinyang Chi Shengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He praised himself lavishly, and many respected court officials rallied to him. He formed close ties with Vice Director Xie Hun and Chief of Jinyang Chi Shengshi.

sentences.zh: 及鎮江陵，豫州舊府多割以自隨，請僧施為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Jiangling he attached much of the old Yu Province headquarters to himself and requested Shengshi as Colonel of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When he took Jiangling he pulled much of the old Yu Province staff to himself and asked that Shengshi be made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 帝知毅終為異端，心密圖之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew that Yi would ultimately prove a rebel and secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew Yi would eventually turn rebel and secretly laid plans against him.

sentences.zh: 毅至西，稱疾篤，表求從弟兗州刺史藩以為副貳，帝偽許焉。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and memorialized asking that his younger male cousin Fan, Inspector of Yan Province, be made his deputy. The Emperor falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and asked that his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yan Province, be made his deputy. The Emperor pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，藩入朝，帝命收藩及謝混，並賜死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Fan entered court. The Emperor ordered Fan and Xie Hun seized, and both were granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fan came to court. The Emperor had Fan and Xie Hun arrested, and both were put to death.

sentences.zh: 自表討毅，又假黃鉞，率諸軍西征。

translations.literal: He memorialized on his own authority to attack Yi, was again granted the yellow axe, and led the armies west.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on his own authority to attack Yi, was again granted the yellow axe, and marched west at the head of the armies.

sentences.zh: 以前鎮軍將軍司馬休之為平西將軍、荊州刺史，兗州刺史道憐鎮丹徒，豫州刺史諸葛長人監太尉留府事，加太尉司馬丹陽尹劉穆之建威將軍，配以實力。

translations.literal: Former General Who Pacifies the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing Province; Liu Daolin, Inspector of Yan Province, garrisoned Dantu; Zhuge Changren, Inspector of Yu Province, oversaw the headquarters left at the Grand Commandant's office; and Grand Commandant Marshal Liu Muzhi, Chief of Jinyang, was added the title General Who Establishes Might, each assigned real forces.
translations.idiomatic: Former General Who Pacifies the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing Province; Liu Daolin of Yan Province held Dantu; Zhuge Changren of Yu Province oversaw the capital headquarters; and Grand Commandant Marshal Liu Muzhi, Chief of Jinyang, was made General Who Establishes Might, each with real troops under command.

sentences.zh: 壬午，發建鄴，遣參軍王鎮惡、龍驤將軍蒯恩前襲江陵，克之，毅及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: On the renwu day he departed Jiankang and sent staff officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon Cavalry General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling. They captured it, and Yi and his partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day he left Jiankang and sent staff officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon Cavalry General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling. They took the city, and Yi and his followers were all executed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝至江陵，分荊州十郡為湘州，帝仍進督焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Emperor reached Jiangling, divided ten commanderies of Jing Province to form Xiang Province, and continued to command it himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Emperor reached Jiangling, carved ten Jing commanderies into Xiang Province, and kept command of it himself.

sentences.zh: 以西陽太守朱齡石為益州刺史，使伐蜀。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Zhu Lingshi was made Inspector of Yi Province and sent to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiyang, was made Inspector of Yi Province and sent to conquer Shu.

sentences.zh: 晉帝進帝太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Jin Emperor promoted the Emperor to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province, adding a feather canopy, drum escort, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Emperor promoted him to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province, adding a feather canopy, drum escort, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乙丑，帝至自江陵。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the second month of the ninth year the Emperor returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the second month in the ninth year the Emperor returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，諸葛長人貪淫驕橫，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuge Changren had been greedy, licentious, and arrogant, and the Emperor had always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changren had long been greedy, licentious, and overbearing, and the Emperor had always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅既誅，長人謂所親曰：「昔年醢彭越，今年殺韓信，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi was executed, Changren told those close to him: "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they killed Han Xin. Disaster is coming.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yi was executed, Changren told his intimates, "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they killed Han Xin. Disaster is near.

sentences.zh: 」將謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He began plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝克期至都，而每淹留不進。

translations.literal: The Emperor set a date to reach the capital, yet each time delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fixed a date to reach the capital, yet each time delayed and did not come.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下，頻日奉候於新亭，長人亦驟出。

translations.literal: From the grandees down, men came day after day to pay their respects at Xinting, and Changren also went out frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and officials came day after day to pay their respects at Xinting, and Changren too went out often.

sentences.zh: 既而帝輕舟密至，已還東府矣。

translations.literal: Then the Emperor arrived secretly in a light boat and was already back at the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Emperor slipped in by light boat and was already back at the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 長人到門，引前，卻人閑語，凡平生言所不盡者，皆與及之，長人甚悅。

translations.literal: When Changren reached the gate he was summoned in. The Emperor dismissed the attendants and spoke with him privately, taking up every matter they had never fully discussed in life. Changren was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Changren came to the gate he was summoned in. The Emperor dismissed the attendants and spoke with him privately, taking up every matter they had never fully aired. Changren was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝已密命左右丁旿自幔後出，於坐拉焉，死於床側。

translations.literal: The Emperor had secretly ordered his attendant Ding Wu to come out from behind the curtain, seize Changren where he sat, and kill him beside the bed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had secretly ordered his attendant Ding Wu to slip out from behind the curtain, seize Changren where he sat, and kill him beside the bed.

sentences.zh: 輿屍付廷尉，並誅其弟黎人。

translations.literal: The corpse was sent to the Court of Justice, and his younger brother Liren was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: The body was sent to the Court of Justice, and his younger brother Liren was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 旿驍勇有力，時人語曰，「勿跋扈，付丁旿」。

translations.literal: Wu was fierce and strong. People of the time said, "Do not be arrogant—leave it to Ding Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wu was fierce and strong. People said at the time, "Don't play the tyrant—leave it to Ding Wu."

sentences.zh: 先是，山湖川澤皆為豪強所奪，百姓薪采漁釣，皆責稅直，至是禁斷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been seized by the powerful families. The people were charged fees even for gathering firewood, fishing, and cutting reeds. Now this was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been seized by powerful families. Even gathering firewood, fishing, and cutting reeds were taxed. Now that was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時人居未一，帝上表定制，於是依界土斷，惟徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者不在斷例。

translations.literal: The people were not yet settled in their places. The Emperor memorialized to set fixed rules, and thereupon resettlement was carried out by territorial boundaries, except for those from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces living at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: The people were not yet settled. The Emperor memorialized to fix the rules, and resettlement was carried out by territorial boundaries, except for those from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces living at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣，多所並省。

translations.literal: Many displaced commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many displaced commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.

sentences.zh: 以帝領鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was appointed concurrently General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was also made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 帝固讓太傅、揚州牧及班劍，奉還黃鉞。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor, Governor of Yang Province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor, Governor of Yang Province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱齡石平蜀，斬譙縱，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded Qiao Zong, and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded Qiao Zong, and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 九月，晉帝以帝平齊、定盧循功，封帝次子義真為桂陽縣公；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for the Emperor's merit in pacifying Qi and settling Lu Xun, the Jin Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's second son Yizhen as Duke of Guiyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, for merit in pacifying Qi and settling Lu Xun, the Jin Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's second son Yizhen as Duke of Guiyang;

sentences.zh: 並重申前命，授帝太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: and again repeated the earlier command, appointing him Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province, with feather canopy, drum escort, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: and again repeated the earlier command, appointing him Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province with feather canopy, drum escort, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 將吏百僚敦勸，乃受羽葆、鼓吹、班劍，餘固辭。

translations.literal: Generals, officials, and the hundred offices urged him repeatedly. He then accepted the feather canopy, drum escort, and ceremonial swords, but firmly declined the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, officials, and the whole court urged him repeatedly. He accepted the feather canopy, drum escort, and ceremonial swords, but firmly declined the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，息人簡役，築東府城，起府舍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he rested the people and reduced corvée labor, built the city of the Eastern Headquarters, and erected its offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he rested the people and reduced corvée labor, built the Eastern Headquarters city, and raised its offices.

sentences.zh: 帝以荊州刺史司馬休之宗室之重，又得江、漢人心，疑其有異志；

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Sima Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jing Province, weighty as a member of the imperial clan and holder of the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions, and suspected him of divergent intent;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor considered Sima Xiuzhi of Jing Province weighty as a member of the imperial clan and a man who held the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions, and suspected him of disloyal intent;

sentences.zh: 而休之子譙王文思在都，招聚輕俠，帝執送休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's son, Prince of Qiao Wensi, was at the capital gathering rowdies. The Emperor seized him and sent him to Xiuzhi, leaving Xiuzhi to deal with him as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's son Prince of Qiao Wensi was at the capital gathering rowdies. The Emperor seized him and sent him to Xiuzhi, leaving him to handle the matter himself.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，並與帝書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wensi and also wrote the Emperor a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wensi and wrote the Emperor a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，帝收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並賜死，率眾西討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year the Emperor arrested Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu, granted both death, and led his forces west in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year the Emperor arrested Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu, had both put to death, and marched west at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 復假黃鉞，領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again granted the yellow axe and held concurrently the post of Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted the yellow axe and held the post of Inspector of Jing Province concurrently.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍道憐監留府事。

translations.literal: General of the Center Liu Daolin was left to oversee the headquarters remaining at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Center Liu Daolin was left to oversee affairs at the capital headquarters.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳，並罪狀帝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own defense and also listed the Emperor's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own defense and also charged the Emperor with crimes.

sentences.zh: 休之府錄事參軍韓延之有幹用才，帝未至江陵，密書招之。

translations.literal: Han YanZhi, Recording Officer on Xiuzhi's staff, was a man of capable talent. Before the Emperor reached Jiangling he wrote secretly to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Han YanZhi, Recording Officer on Xiuzhi's staff, was a capable man. Before the Emperor reached Jiangling he wrote secretly to win him over.

sentences.zh: 延之報書曰：「承親率戎馬，遠履西偏，闔境士庶，莫不惶駭。

translations.literal: YanZhi replied: "I learn that you personally lead your horses and chariots far into the western frontier. Gentry and commoners throughout the region are all struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: YanZhi replied, "I learn that you personally lead your army far into the western frontier. Gentry and commoners throughout the region are all struck with terror.

sentences.zh: 辱疏，知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: I am honored by your letter and understand that this concerns the affair of the Prince of Qiao. That only adds to my sighs.
translations.idiomatic: I am honored by your letter and understand that this concerns the Prince of Qiao. That only deepens my sighs.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，款懷待物，以公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Sima the Pacifier of the West embodies the state's loyalty, treats men with sincere goodwill, and because you have the merit of restoring the dynasty, state and family rely upon you. He extended virtue and entrusted sincerity, consulting you in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Sima the Pacifier of the West embodies the state's loyalty and treats men with sincere goodwill. Because you have the merit of restoring the dynasty, state and family rely upon you. He extended you virtue and entrusted you with sincerity, consulting you in every matter.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao, though impeached for a minor matter, still memorialized on his own to yield his rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiao, though impeached for a minor matter, still memorialized on his own to yield his rank;

sentences.zh: 況以大過而當默邪！

translations.literal: how much less should one keep silent when faced with a great fault!
translations.idiomatic: how much less should one keep silent when faced with a great fault!

sentences.zh: 來示雲，'處懷期物，自有由來'。

translations.literal: Your letter says, 'To treat men with an eye to future gain has its own origins.'
translations.idiomatic: Your letter says, 'To treat men with an eye to future gain has its own origins.'

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啖人以利，真可謂'處懷期物'者矣。

translations.literal: Now you attack another man's lord and feed men with profit—this is truly what may be called 'treating men with an eye to future gain.'
translations.idiomatic: Now you attack another man's lord and feed men with profit—this is truly what may be called treating men with an eye to future gain.

sentences.zh: 劉藩死於閶闔之門，諸葛斃於左右之手，甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵，遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以為得算，良所恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan died at Changhe Gate, Zhuge was killed by attendants' hands. With sweet words you deceive the regional lords, then surprise them with light troops. Thus there are no sincere men at the banquet, and no self-confident lords beyond the borders. To think this clever strategy—how shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died at Changhe Gate, Zhuge was killed by attendants' hands. With sweet words you deceive the regional lords, then surprise them with light troops. Thus there are no sincere men at the banquet and no confident lords beyond the borders. To call this clever strategy is shameful.

sentences.zh: 吾雖鄙劣，嘗聞道于君子，以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎？

translations.literal: Though I am base and mean, I have heard the way from gentlemen. With the Pacifier of the West's supreme virtue, how could there fail to be ministers who would give their lives?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am base and mean, I have heard the way from gentlemen. With the Pacifier of the West's supreme virtue, how could there fail to be ministers who would give their lives?

sentences.zh: 假天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪游於地下。

translations.literal: If Heaven does not long prolong chaos and the nine streams run turbid, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven does not long prolong chaos and the age runs turbid, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong.

sentences.zh: 不復多云。

translations.literal: I shall say no more."
translations.idiomatic: I shall say no more."

sentences.zh: 」帝視書歎息，以示將佐曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his generals and aides, saying: "Serving one's lord should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his generals and aides. "Serving one's lord should be like this," he said.

sentences.zh: 三月，軍次江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month the army halted at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army halted at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，雍州刺史魯宗之負力好亂，且慮不為帝容，常為讖曰：「魚登日，輔帝室。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Zongzhi, Inspector of Yong Province, relied on his strength and loved disorder. Fearing the Emperor would not tolerate him, he often made a prophecy: "When the fish ascends the sun, it assists the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lu Zongzhi, Inspector of Yong Province, relied on his strength and loved disorder. Fearing the Emperor would not tolerate him, he often repeated a prophecy: "When the fish ascends the sun, it assists the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 」與休之相結。

translations.literal: " He allied with Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " He allied with Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 至是，率其子竟陵太守軌會于江陵。

translations.literal: At this he led his son Gui, Administrator of Jingling, to rendezvous at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Now he led his son Gui, Administrator of Jingling, to rendezvous at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 帝濟江，休之眾潰，與軌等奔襄陽，江陵平。

translations.literal: The Emperor crossed the river; Xiuzhi's masses collapsed; with Gui and the rest he fled to Xiangyang, and Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor crossed the river. Xiuzhi's army broke and fled with Gui and the others to Xiangyang. Jiangling was taken.

sentences.zh: 加領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Chief of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Chief of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 將拜南蠻，遇四廢日，佐史鄭鮮之等白遷日，不許。

translations.literal: When he was about to take office as Chief of the Southern Man, it fell on a day of the four prohibitions; the clerks Zheng Xianzhi and the rest reported asking to move the day—he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to take office as Chief of the Southern Man, the day fell under the four prohibitions. His clerks Zheng Xianzhi and the others asked to postpone it. He refused.

sentences.zh: 下書開寬大之恩。

translations.literal: He issued a document opening wide and generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict proclaiming clemency and relief.

sentences.zh: 四月，進軍襄陽，休之等奔姚興。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he advanced the army to Xiangyang; Xiuzhi and the rest fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army marched on Xiangyang. Xiuzhi and his followers fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 晉帝復申前令，授太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，封第三子義隆為北彭城縣公。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor again earnestly repeated the earlier commands, appointing him Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court entry, no naming in supportive obeisance, adding the forward feather-canopy and martial music, setting four Left and Right Chiefs of Staff, Marshals, and Attending Gentlemen, and enfeoffing his third son Yilong as Duke of North Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor again pressed the earlier honors on him: Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court, no naming in obeisance, forward feather-canopy and martial music, four chiefs of staff, marshals, and attending gentlemen on left and right, and enfeoffment of his third son Yilong as Duke of North Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，帝至自江陵，奉還黃鉞，固辭太傅、州牧、前部羽葆、鼓吹，其餘受命。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi in the eighth month the Emperor arrived from Jiangling, returned the yellow battle-axe, firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor, forward feather-canopy and martial music, and accepted the rest of the commands.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi in the eighth month the Emperor returned from Jiangling. He gave back the yellow battle-axe and refused Grand Tutor, Governor, and the forward canopy and music, but accepted the other honors.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，晉帝詔帝依舊辟士，加領平北將軍、兗州刺史，增督南秦，凡二十二州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year the Jin emperor ordered the Emperor to recruit gentlemen as before, additionally made him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yanzhou, and increased his supervision to include Southern Qin—for a total of twenty-two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year the Jin emperor ordered the Emperor to recruit gentlemen as before, made him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yanzhou, and extended his command to Southern Qin—for twenty-two provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 帝以平北文武寡少，不宜別置，於是罷平北府，以並大府。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered that the civil and military staff of Pacifying the North were few and should not be set up separately; thereupon he abolished the Pacifying-the-North headquarters and merged it into the great headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that Pacifying the North had too few officials and soldiers to warrant a separate headquarters, so he abolished that office and merged it into his main headquarters.

sentences.zh: 三月，加帝中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor was made Grand Commander of Court and Country.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Grand Commander of Court and Country.

sentences.zh: 初，帝平齊，仍有定關、洛意，遇盧循侵逼，故寢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor had pacified Qi, he still had the intent to settle Guan and Luo; it happened that Lu Xun pressed in invasion, and therefore the affair was laid aside.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Qi he still meant to recover the Guan and Luo region, but Lu Xun's invasion forced him to set that plan aside.

sentences.zh: 及荊、雍平，乃謀外略。

translations.literal: Once Jing and Yong were pacified, he then plotted outward expansion.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong secure, he turned to campaigns abroad.

sentences.zh: 會姚興死，子泓新立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂。

translations.literal: It happened that Yao Xing died; his son Hong had newly established himself; brothers killed one another; Guanzhong was disturbed and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing died. His son Hong had just taken the throne; brothers turned on one another and Guanzhong fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，帝表伐關、洛，乃戒嚴北討，加領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day yichou in the fourth month the Emperor memorialized to campaign against Guan and Luo; thereupon he ordered martial readiness for a northern expedition and was additionally made General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Si and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou in the fourth month the Emperor memorialized for a campaign against Guan and Luo, ordered the army to prepare for a northern expedition, and was also made General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 以世子為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Governor of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Governor of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以義聲懷遠，奉琅邪王北伐。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished with righteous renown to win the distant and to lead the Prince of Langye on a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to win the distant lands by righteous fame and to lead the Prince of Langye north in person.

sentences.zh: 五月，廬江霍山崩，獲六鍾，獻之天子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Mount Huo in Lujiang collapsed; six bells were obtained and presented to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Mount Huo in Lujiang collapsed. Six bells were found and sent to the throne.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，加領北雍州刺史，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: On the day guisi he was additionally made Governor of Northern Yong, with forward and rear feather-canopies and martial music; ceremonial swords were increased to forty men.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi he was also made Governor of Northern Yong, with forward and rear canopies, martial music, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，率大眾進發，以世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事，尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi in the eighth month he led the great host forth in advance; the heir was made Central Army General and oversaw the headquarters affairs left with the Grand Commandant; Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director, holding concurrently the army marshals of the Overseer Army and Central Army headquarters, entering and dwelling in the Eastern Headquarters, and taking overall charge of inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi in the eighth month he led the main army out. The heir was made Central Army General and oversaw affairs at the Grand Commandant's headquarters. Liu Muzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, became Left Vice Director and took charge of the Overseer Army and Central Army staffs at the Eastern Headquarters, directing affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝至彭城，加領北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor reached Pengcheng and was additionally made Governor of Northern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor reached Pengcheng and was also made Governor of Northern Xu.

sentences.zh: 十月，眾軍至洛，圍金墉，降之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the host of armies reached Luo, besieged Jinyong, and received its surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army reached Luoyang, besieged Jinyong, and took its surrender.

sentences.zh: 修復晉五陵，置守衛。

translations.literal: The five tombs of Jin were restored and guards were set.
translations.idiomatic: The five Jin imperial tombs were restored and guards were posted.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬申，晉帝加帝位相國、總百揆、揚州牧，封十郡為宋公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱、遠遊冠、綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, the Jin emperor advanced the Emperor to Chief Minister, overseer of the hundred duties and Governor of Yangzhou, enfeoffed ten commanderies as Duke of Song, provided the rites of the nine bestowals, added imperial seals and cord, the far-wandering cap, and the green sash and cord; his rank was above the feudal princes and kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, the Jin emperor made him Chief Minister, overseer of all government and Governor of Yangzhou, Duke of Song over ten commanderies, with the Nine Bestowals, imperial seals and cord, the far-wandering cap, and the Chief Minister's green sash, ranking him above all princes and kings.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The mandate document says:
translations.idiomatic: The mandate reads:

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，仰纘洪基，夷羿乘釁，蕩覆王室，越在南鄙，遷於九江。

translations.literal: I, being dull and dim, look up to continue the great foundation; Yi of the east seized the opportunity; he overturned and capsized the royal house; he crossed to the southern marches and moved to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and weak, yet I uphold the great foundation. Yi seized his chance, overthrew the throne, fled south, and moved the court to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 宗祀絕饗，人神無位，提挈群凶，寄命江浦，則我祖宗之烈，奄墜於地，七百之祚，翦焉既傾，若涉巨海，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: The ancestral sacrifices were cut off; men and spirits had no place; I was dragged along with the crowd of villains and entrusted my life to the riverbank—then the blazing achievement of our ancestors suddenly fell to the ground; the fortune of seven hundred years was already cut down and toppled; as if crossing a great sea, I knew not what to cross to.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral rites ceased; gods and men were displaced. I was dragged along with rebels and lived as a refugee on the river. Our ancestors' legacy collapsed; seven hundred years of fortune fell. I was as one drowning in a great sea, with no shore in sight.

sentences.zh: 天未絕晉，誕育英輔，振厥弛維，再造區宇，興亡繼絕，俾昏作明，元勳至德，朕實攸賴。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet cut off Jin; it brought forth an heroic assistant; he shook the slackened cords and remade the realm within the four quarters; he continued the dying and restored the cut off, making the dim bright; in primordial merit and utmost virtue—I truly rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not yet end Jin. It sent a great helper who tightened the loosened bonds, remade the realm, restored the fallen, and brought light to the dark. In supreme merit and virtue I truly rely on him.

sentences.zh: 今將授公典策，其敬聽朕命：乃者，桓玄肆僭，滔天泯夏，拔本塞源，顛蹶六位，庶僚俛眉，四方莫恤。

translations.literal: Now I will confer on the Duke the canonical mandate; respectfully hear my command: in former days Huan Xuan ran riot in usurpation, flooding Heaven and extinguishing Xia; he uprooted the root and blocked the source, overturning the six positions; the many officials bowed their brows; the four directions none consoled.
translations.idiomatic: Now I confer the canonical mandate upon him. Hear my command: Huan Xuan usurped power, overwhelmed Heaven, and destroyed the dynasty. He uprooted the state and overturned the cosmic order. Officials bowed in fear; none could save the realm.

sentences.zh: 公精貫朝日，氣陵虹蜺，奮其靈武，大殲群慝，克復皇邑，奉歆神只。

translations.literal: The Duke's essence penetrated the morning sun; his spirit towered over the rainbow; he roused his spiritual martial and greatly slaughtered the crowd of villains; he recovered the imperial city and presented offerings to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's spirit matched the sun; his valor reached the heavens. He crushed the rebels, recovered the capital, and restored the emperor to the spirits' altar.

sentences.zh: 此公之大節始于勤王者也。

translations.literal: This is the Duke's great integrity, beginning in service to the kingly cause.
translations.idiomatic: This was his first great act of loyalty, when he served the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 授律群後，泝流長騖，薄伐崢嶸，獻捷南郢，大憝折首，群逆畢夷，三光旋采，舊物反正。

translations.literal: He received the law among the lords, went upstream in long gallop, made light campaign against the lofty peaks, presented victory at Southern Jing; the great villain broke his head; the crowd of rebels were all leveled; the three luminaries turned their light; old things returned to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: He took command among the lords, marched upstream, struck the highlands, and won victory at Southern Jing. The chief rebel was destroyed and all enemies swept away. The realm was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 出藩入輔，弘茲保弼，阜財利用，繁殖黎元，編戶歲滋，疆宇日啟，導德明刑，四境有截。

translations.literal: Going out to the frontier and entering as assistant, he enlarged this protection and support; he enriched goods and benefited use, bred and raised the common people; registered households yearly increased; the frontier realm daily opened; he guided virtue and clarified punishments—the four borders had boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: As minister at court and lord abroad, he enriched the people, increased households, extended the borders, governed by virtue, and brought peace to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑負眾，僭盜三齊，介恃遐阻，仍為邊害，公搜乘秣馬，敻入遠疆，沖櫓四臨，萬雉俱潰，拓土三千，申威龍漠。

translations.literal: The Xianbei bore their masses and usurped and stole the three Qi; relying on distant barriers, they again became border poison; the Duke gathered chariots and fed horses, entered the far frontier; assault towers looked down on four sides; ten thousand ramparts all collapsed; he extended territory three thousand li and declared authority on the Dragon Desert.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei seized the three Qi and, from their distant strongholds, plagued the borders. The Duke gathered his forces and drove deep into the frontier. His assault towers surrounded the enemy on every side; fortress after fortress fell. Three thousand li of territory were won and his authority proclaimed across the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 盧循祅凶，伺隙五嶺，侵覆江、豫，矢及王城，國議遷都之規，家獻徙卜之計，公乘轅南濟，義形於色，運奇攄略，英謨不世，狡寇窮衄，喪旗宵遁，俾我畿甸，拯於將墜。

translations.literal: Lu Xun, demonic and vicious, watched for a gap in the five ridges, overthrowing and covering Jiang and Yu; his arrows reached the royal city; the state discussed plans to move the capital; families offered plans to move house; the Duke rode the shafts south across the river; righteousness showed in his face; he spread strategy and moved wonders; his heroic plan was not of the age; the cunning bandit was driven to extremity and lost his banners fleeing by night; he made our capital region be saved from about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun the rebel watched his chance in the five ridges, swept through Jiang and Yu, and threatened the capital itself. Some urged moving the capital; others urged moving their households. The Duke crossed the river in person, righteous wrath on his face. By unmatched strategy he drove the rebel to flight by night and saved the capital from ruin.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 追奔逐北，揚旍江濆，偏旅浮海，指日遄至，番禺之功，俘級萬數，左裏之捷，鳥散魚潰，元凶遠竄，傳首萬里。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing and chasing the north, he raised banners on the river's bank; a detached brigade floated on the sea and in a day arrived swiftly; at the achievement of Panyu the captives and severed heads were in the tens of thousands; at the victory of Zuoli the birds scattered and fish collapsed; the chief villain fled far; his head was transmitted ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing enemy along the river and sent a fleet across the sea that arrived within days. At Panyu tens of thousands were captured; at Zuoli the enemy broke and scattered like birds and fish. The chief rebel fled far away; his head was sent a thousand leagues.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 劉毅叛換，負釁西夏，陵上罔主，志肆奸暴，公禦軌以刑，消之不日，罪人斯得，荊、衡甯晏。

translations.literal: Liu Yi changed in rebellion, bearing guilt in the western Xia; he insulted above and deceived the sovereign; his will ran riot in treacherous violence; the Duke controlled the track with punishment; within not a day he extinguished them; the guilty man was thereby obtained; Jing and Heng were clear and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi rebelled in the west, insulted the throne, and gave free rein to treachery and violence. The Duke struck with the law and destroyed him within a day. The rebel was taken and Jing and Heng were pacified.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 譙縱怙亂，寇竊一隅，王化阻閡，三巴淪溺，公指命偏帥，授以良圖，陵波憑湍，致屆井絡，僭豎伏鑕，梁、岷草偃。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong relied on disorder; he bandited and stole one corner; royal transformation was blocked and barred; the three Ba were drowned and submerged; the Duke pointed and ordered a detached army; he entrusted them with a good plan; crossing waves and floating rapids, they arrived at the well rope; the usurping chieftain was made to bow at the executioner's block; Liang and Min lay down like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong seized a corner of the realm, blocked royal authority, and drowned the three Ba in rebellion. The Duke sent a detached force with a sound plan. They crossed the rapids, reached the heart of the region, executed the usurper, and pacified Liang and Min.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 馬休、魯宗，阻兵內侮，驅率二方，連旗稱亂，公投袂星言，研其上略，江津之師，勢踰風電，回旆沔川，實繁震懾，二叛奔迸，荊、雍來蘇。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu and Lu Zong blocked the army and insulted within; they drove and led the two regions; they linked banners and called it rebellion; the Duke threw his sleeves and spoke like a star; he studied their upper strategy; the army at the river crossing—its momentum exceeded wind and lightning; turning the banners on the Mian River, the reality was abundant shock and fear; the two rebels ran and bolted; Jing and Yong came back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu and Lu Zong took up arms in the interior, rallied two regions, and raised rebellion. The Duke moved like a star, outgeneraled them, and struck at the river crossing with the force of wind and lightning. The rebels fled; Jing and Yong revived under his rule.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 永嘉不競，四夷擅華，五都傾蕩，山陵幽辱，祖宗懷沒世之憤，遺甿有匪風之思，公遠齊阿衡納隍之仁，近同小白滅亡之恥，鞠旅陳師，赫然大號，分命群帥，北徇司、兗，許、鄭風靡，鞏、洛載清，百年榛穢，一朝掃滌。

translations.literal: The Yongjia reign did not compete; the four barbarians usurped China; the five capitals were overturned and shaken; mountains and tombs suffered hidden insult; the ancestors harbored the indignation of perishing in the age; the remnant people had the thought of unrighteous wind; the Duke from afar aligned with the benevolence of the Yi-Yin minister who received the drowning; near at hand he shared the shame of the small white who extinguished extinction; he gathered troops and arrayed the army; he blazed forth with a great proclamation; he divided commands to the crowd of marshals and marched north along Si and Yan; Xu and Zheng bent to the wind; Gong and Luo were loaded with clarity; a hundred years of thorn and filth—in one morning were swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongjia the barbarians had seized China; the five capitals were lost; the tombs lay in shame. The dead cried for vengeance; the living yearned for restoration. The Duke matched Yi Yin who saved the drowning king and the Duke of Qi who avenged a fallen state. He raised his army, proclaimed a great crusade, and sent his generals north to Si and Yan. Xu and Zheng submitted; Gong and Luo were cleared. A century of ruin was swept away in a morning.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 公有康宇內之勳，重之以明德。

translations.literal: The Duke has the achievement of bringing peace within the four seas, heavy with bright virtue besides.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke has brought peace to the realm, and his virtue matches his deeds.

sentences.zh: 爰初發跡，則奇謨冠古，電擊強祅，則鋒無前對，聿寧東畿，大造黔首。

translations.literal: When he first set forth on the trail, then his strange plans crowned antiquity; lightning struck strong demons; his edge had none before it to face; he tranquilly settled the eastern capital region and greatly made the black-headed people.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rise his plans surpassed the ancients. He struck down mighty rebels with lightning speed, pacified the eastern capital, and saved the people.

sentences.zh: 若乃草昧經綸，化融于歲計，扶危靜亂，道固于苞桑。

translations.literal: As for grass and darkness in the warp and woof of rule, transformation melted within the year's reckoning; propping peril and quieting disorder—the Way was firm in the mulberry bud.
translations.idiomatic: In founding the state he transformed the realm year by year; in saving it from peril he made the Way firm as the mulberry root.

sentences.zh: 蠲削煩苛，較若畫一，淳風美化，盈塞區宇。

translations.literal: He abolished and cut away troublesome severity, comparing as if drawn with one stroke; pure wind and beautiful teaching filled and blocked the realm within the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He cut away harsh laws with uniform fairness and spread pure civilization throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 是以絕域獻琛，遐夷納贐，王略所宣，九服率從。

translations.literal: Therefore the cut-off domains presented treasures; distant barbarians brought tribute gifts; where the royal plan was proclaimed, the nine services followed in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the farthest lands sent tribute and all the nine regions followed his rule.

sentences.zh: 雖文命之東漸西被，咎繇之邁於種德，何以尚茲。

translations.literal: Though Yu the Great's eastward flow and westward spread, and Gao Yao's surpassing in planting virtue—how could they be placed above this?
translations.idiomatic: Not even Yu the Great's reach east and west, nor Gao Yao's virtue in planting goodness, could surpass this.

sentences.zh: 朕聞先王之宰世也，庸勳尊賢，建侯胙土，褒以寵章，崇其徽物，所以協輔皇室，永隆藩屏。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the former kings governed the world, they employed merit and honored the worthy, established marquises and enfeoffed with soil, praised them with favoring seals, and exalted their emblematic objects—thereby to assist and support the royal house and forever elevate the frontier screen.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ancient kings governed by honoring merit and the worthy, enfeoffing lords and rewarding them with honors, so that they might support the throne and guard the realm forever.

sentences.zh: 故曲阜光啟，遂荒徐宅，營丘表海，四履有聞。

translations.literal: Therefore Qufu was brightly opened and then the wilds of Xu were extended; Yingqiu faced the sea and on four legs there was renown.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qufu was glorified and Xu extended; Yingqiu looked to the sea and its fame reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 其在襄王，亦賴匡霸，又命晉文，備物光賜。

translations.literal: In the case of King Xiang, he also relied on rectifying hegemony; again he ordered Duke Wen of Jin, and complete objects were brightly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang too relied on hegemons to restore order; he richly rewarded Duke Wen of Jin with full honors.

sentences.zh: 惟公道冠前烈，勳高振古，而殊典未飾，朕甚懵焉！

translations.literal: Only the Duke's Way crowns former blazing deeds; his achievement is high and shakes antiquity—yet the extraordinary canon has not been adorned; I am very dull indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's virtue surpasses the ancients and his merit shakes history, yet the highest honors have not been granted. I am deeply at fault!

sentences.zh: 今進授相國，以徐州之彭城沛蘭陵下邳淮陽山陽廣陵、兗州之高平魯泰山十郡封公為宋公，錫茲玄土，苴以白茅，爰定爾居，用建塚社。

translations.literal: Now I advance and confer Chief Minister, with the ten commanderies of Pengcheng, Pei, Lanling, Xiapi, Huaiyang, Shanyang, and Guangling in Xuzhou, and Gaoping, Lu, and Taishan in Yanzhou, and enfeoff the Duke as Duke of Song; bestow this dark earth, wrap it with white thatch, thereby fix your dwelling, and use it to establish the altar of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Now I make him Chief Minister and Duke of Song over ten commanderies: Pengcheng, Pei, Lanling, Xiapi, Huaiyang, Shanyang, and Guangling in Xu, and Gaoping, Lu, and Taishan in Yan. I bestow this sacred earth wrapped in white thatch, that he may fix his dwelling and establish his altar of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 昔晉、鄭啟藩，入作卿士，周、召保傅，出總二南，內外之任，公實兼之。

translations.literal: In former times Jin and Zheng opened the frontier and entered to serve as chief ministers; Zhou and Shao protected and tutored, going out to oversee the two souths—of inner and outer weight, the Duke truly combines them.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Jin and Zheng were frontier lords who became chief ministers; the dukes of Zhou and Shao tutored the heir and governed abroad. The Duke unites both roles.

sentences.zh: 今命使持節、兼太尉、尚書左僕射晉寧縣五等男湛授相國印綬，宋公璽紱，使持節、兼司空、散騎常侍、尚書陽遂鄉侯泰授宋公茅土，金虎符第一至第五左，竹使符第一至第十左。

translations.literal: Now I order the commissioner with credentials, concurrently Grand Commandant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Baron of the Fifth Rank of Jinning County Zhan, to confer the Chief Minister's seals and cord and the Duke of Song's seals and sash; the commissioner with credentials, concurrently Minister of Works, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Master of Writing, Marquis of Yangsui Township Tai, to confer on the Duke of Song the thatch earth, the golden tiger tally first through fifth on the left, and the bamboo envoy tally first through tenth on the left.
translations.idiomatic: I send Commissioner Zhan, Grand Commandant and Left Vice Director, Baron of Jinning, to confer the Chief Minister's seals and cord and the Duke of Song's seals and sash. I send Commissioner Tai, Minister of Works, Regular Attendant, and Master of Writing, Marquis of Yangsui, to confer the enfeoffment earth, golden tiger tallies one through five on the left, and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten on the left.

sentences.zh: 相國位無不總，禮絕朝班，居常之名，宜與事革。

translations.literal: The Chief Minister's position—none he does not oversee; his rites cut off the court ranks; the name used in ordinary times should change with the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Minister oversees all affairs and stands above the court. His ordinary title should change with his new office.

sentences.zh: 其以相國總百揆，去錄尚書之號；

translations.literal: Let him as Chief Minister oversee the hundred duties and remove the title "Recording the Masters of Writing";
translations.idiomatic: Let him as Chief Minister oversee all government and drop the title Recording the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 上送所假節、侍中貂蟬、中外都督太傅太尉印綬、豫章公印策；

translations.literal: send up the borrowed tally, Attendant's sable cicada, seals and cord of Grand Commander of Court and Country, Grand Tutor and Grand Commandant, and the Duke of Yuzhang's seal and mandate document;
translations.idiomatic: return the borrowed tally, Attendant's regalia, seals of Grand Commander, Grand Tutor, and Grand Commandant, and the Duke of Yuzhang's seal and mandate;

sentences.zh: 進揚州刺史為牧，領征西將軍、司豫北徐雍四州刺史如故。

translations.literal: advance him to Governor of Yangzhou, holding concurrently General Who Campaigns West and the four provinces of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong as before.
translations.idiomatic: advance him to Governor of Yangzhou, retaining General Who Campaigns West and the governorships of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 公紀綱禮度，萬國是式，乘介蹈方，罔有遷志，是用錫公大路、戎路各一，玄牡二駟；

translations.literal: The Duke's warp and woof of rites and measure are the model for the ten thousand states; riding the go-between and treading the square, he has no shifting will—therefore he is bestowed a great chariot and a military chariot, each one, and dark stallions in a team of four;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's governance is the model for all states. He holds firm to the right path and never wavers. Therefore he is granted a great chariot and a war chariot, each with a team of four dark stallions;

sentences.zh: 公抑末敦本，務農重積，采蘩實殷，稼穡惟阜，是用錫公袞冕之服，赤舄副焉；

translations.literal: The Duke restrains the branch and honors the root, devotes himself to agriculture and values accumulation; he gathers duckweed and the harvest is abundant; grain crops alone are lofty—therefore he is bestowed the robe and cap of the highest rank, with red shoes as adjunct;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke honors the root over the branch, devotes himself to farming, and gathers rich harvests. For this he is granted the highest robe and cap, with red shoes;

sentences.zh: 公閑邪納正，移風改俗，陶鈞品物，如樂之和，是用錫公軒縣之樂、六佾之舞；

translations.literal: The Duke checks evil and receives the upright, shifts the wind and changes custom, potters and balances all things like the harmony of music—therefore he is bestowed the music of the elevated bells and the dance of six rows;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke corrects evil and upholds the right, transforms customs, and shapes all things as music shapes harmony. For this he is granted royal music and the six-row dance;

sentences.zh: 公宣美王化，導揚休風，華夷企踵，遠人胥萃，是用錫公朱戶以居；

translations.literal: The Duke proclaims beautiful royal transformation, guides and raises fine wind; Chinese and barbarians stand on tiptoe; distant men all gather—therefore he is bestowed vermilion doors to dwell in;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke spreads royal civilization and fine customs; Chinese and barbarians alike look to him, and distant peoples gather. For this he is granted vermilion doors for his dwelling;

sentences.zh: 公官方任能，網羅幽滯，九皋辭野，髦士盈朝，是用錫公納陛以登；

translations.literal: The Duke in official posts employs the able; his net gathers the hidden and stagnant; from the nine marshes they leave the wild; eminent gentlemen fill the court—therefore he is bestowed the hidden steps to ascend;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke appoints the able and gathers the neglected; worthy men fill the court. For this he is granted the hidden steps to ascend;

sentences.zh: 公當軸處中，率下以義，式遏寇讎，滌除苛慝，是用錫公虎賁之士三百人；

translations.literal: The Duke at the axle sits in the center, leads those below by righteousness, checks and halts bandit foes, and clears away harsh evil—therefore he is bestowed three hundred tiger-guard warriors;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke holds the center, leads by righteousness, repels enemies, and clears away harsh wrongs. For this he is granted three hundred tiger guards;

sentences.zh: 公明罰恤刑，庶獄詳允，放命幹紀，罔有攸縱，是用錫公鈇鉞各一；

translations.literal: The Duke clarifies punishments and comforts punishments; the many prisons are detailed and true; those who throw off commands and violate discipline—none have a place to flee—therefore he is bestowed an axe and a battle-axe, each one;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke clarifies punishments and judges fairly; rebels and lawbreakers have nowhere to flee. For this he is granted an axe and a ceremonial axe;

sentences.zh: 公龍驤鳳矯，咫尺八紘，括囊四海，折沖無外，是用錫公彤弓一、彤矢百，玈弓十、玈矢千；

translations.literal: The Duke, dragon soaring and phoenix rising, within a foot the eight cords; he bundles the four seas in a sack; repelling the foe without, nothing outside—therefore he is bestowed one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke soars like dragon and phoenix; within a foot he commands the eight directions, holds the four seas in his grasp, and repels every foe abroad. For this he is granted one red bow and a hundred red arrows, ten black bows and a thousand black arrows;

sentences.zh: 公溫恭孝思，致虔禋祀，忠肅之志，儀刑四方，是用錫公秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。

translations.literal: The Duke is warm, respectful, filial, and thoughtful; he brings sincerity to the suburban sacrifices; his loyal and solemn will is the model and law for the ten thousand regions—therefore he is bestowed one jar of black millet wine and libation vessels as adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke is reverent in filial piety and sincere in sacrifice; his loyal devotion is the model for all the realm. For this he is granted sacred wine and libation vessels.

sentences.zh: 宋國置丞相以下，一遵舊儀。

translations.literal: In the state of Song, from Chief Minister down—all follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the state of Song, from Chief Minister down, all offices follow the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 欽哉，其祗服往命，茂對天休，簡恤庶邦，敬敷顯德，以終我高祖之嘉命！

translations.literal: Reverence! Respectfully take the going mandate, abundantly respond to Heaven's blessing, simply comfort the many states, respectfully spread bright virtue, to complete my high ancestor's fine command!
translations.idiomatic: Reverence! Reverently accept this mandate, answer Heaven's blessing, care for the people, spread your bright virtue, and fulfill my high ancestor's command!

sentences.zh: 置宋國侍中、黃門侍郎、尚書左丞，即隨大使奉迎。

translations.literal: Set up in the state of Song Attendant, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, who at once with the great envoy will welcome and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Let Song establish Attendants, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate, and the Left Assistant Director to welcome the envoy at once.

sentences.zh: 枹罕虜乞伏熾盤遣使謁帝，求效力討姚泓，拜為平西將軍、河南公。

translations.literal: The Baoheng barbarian Qifu Chipan sent an envoy to visit the Emperor, requesting to offer strength in attacking Yao Hong; he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan of Baoheng sent envoys to the Emperor offering to join the campaign against Yao Hong. He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，帝以舟師進討，留彭城公義隆鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor advanced by water army in campaign; he left Duke of Pengcheng Yilong to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor marched by river. He left Yilong, Duke of Pengcheng, to guard the city.

sentences.zh: 軍次陳留城，經張良廟，下令以時修飾棟宇致薦焉。

translations.literal: The army halted at Chenliu city; passing Zhang Liang's temple, he ordered that at the proper season the rafters and halls be repaired and offerings presented.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Chenliu. At Zhang Liang's temple the Emperor ordered that the halls be repaired in season and offerings made.

sentences.zh: 晉帝追贈帝祖為太常，父為特進、左光祿大夫，讓不受。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor posthumously enfeoffed the Emperor's grandfather as Minister of Ceremonies and his father as Special Court Advisor and Left Household Master of Light; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor posthumously honored the Emperor's grandfather as Minister of Ceremonies and his father as Special Court Advisor and Left Household Master of Light. The Emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 二月，冠軍將軍檀道濟等軍次潼關。

translations.literal: In the second month Champion General Tan Daoji and others halted at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Tan Daoji and other generals reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰，帝率大軍入河。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen in the third month the Emperor led the great army into the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen in the third month the Emperor led the main army across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝至洛陽，謁晉五陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor reached Luoyang and visited the five tombs of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Emperor reached Luoyang and visited the five Jin imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 七月，至陝，龍驤將軍王鎮惡舟師自河浮渭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Shan; Flying-Dragon General Wang Zhen'e's water army from the river floated onto the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he reached Shan. Wang Zhen'e, Flying-Dragon General, sailed his fleet from the Yellow River onto the Wei.

sentences.zh: 八月，扶風太守沈田子大破姚泓軍于藍田，王鎮惡克長安，禽姚泓。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi greatly defeated Yao Hong's army at Lantian; Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Hong alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shen Tianzi, Administrator of Fufeng, routed Yao Hong's army at Lantian. Wang Zhen'e took Chang'an and captured Hong alive.

sentences.zh: 始義熙九年，歲、鎮、熒惑、太白聚東井，至是而關中平。

translations.literal: From the ninth year of Yixi, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Venus gathered at the Well; by this time Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Since the ninth year of Yixi, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Venus had gathered at the Well constellation. Now Guanzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝至長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 長安豐稔，帑藏盈積，帝先收其彝器、渾儀、土圭、記裏鼓、指南車及秦始皇玉璽送之都；

translations.literal: Chang'an was abundant and the harvest full; the treasury stores were full and accumulated; the Emperor first collected its ritual vessels, armillary sphere, earth square, mile-measuring drum, south-pointing carriage, and the jade seal of Qin Shihuang and sent them to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an was rich and its granaries full. The Emperor first sent its ritual vessels, armillary sphere, earth square, mile-measuring drum, south-pointing carriage, and the jade seal of the First Emperor of Qin to the capital;

sentences.zh: 其餘珍寶珠玉，悉以班賜將帥。

translations.literal: the rest of the precious treasures, pearls, and jade he distributed in bestowal to the marshals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: and distributed the rest of the jewels and treasures among his generals.

sentences.zh: 遷姚宗於江南，送泓斬于建康市。

translations.literal: The Yao clan was moved to the lands south of the river; Hong was sent and beheaded in the market of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao clan was resettled south of the river. Hong was sent to the capital and beheaded in the market at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 謁漢長陵，大會文武於未央殿。

translations.literal: He visited the tomb of the Long Emperor of Han and held a great assembly of civil and military men in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the tomb of Emperor Gaozu of Han and held a great assembly of civil and military officials in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 十月，晉帝詔進宋公爵為王，加十郡益宋國，並前為二十郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Jin emperor ordered that the Duke of the state of Song advance to King, adding ten commanderies to increase the state of Song—for twenty commanderies together with those before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Jin emperor ordered that the Duke of Song advance to King, adding ten commanderies to the state of Song—for twenty commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 其相國、揚州牧、領征西將軍、司豫北徐雍四州刺史如故。

translations.literal: His Chief Minister, Governor of Yangzhou, holding General Who Campaigns West and the four provinces of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong, are as before.
translations.idiomatic: He remains Chief Minister, Governor of Yangzhou, General Who Campaigns West, and governor of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 帝欲息駕長安，經略趙、魏，十一月，前將軍劉穆之卒，乃歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to halt his chariot at Chang'an and plan strategy for Zhao and Wei; in the eleventh month Forward General Liu Muzhi died, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor meant to remain at Chang'an and plan for Zhao and Wei, but in the eleventh month Liu Muzhi, Forward General, died, and he turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚子，發自長安，以桂陽公義真為雍州刺史，鎮長安，留腹心將佐以輔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, he set out from Chang'an; Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was made Governor of Yong, garrisoning Chang'an, and trusted generals and assistants were left to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, he left Chang'an. Yizhen, Duke of Guiyang, was made Governor of Yong and garrisoned Chang'an, with trusted generals left to assist him.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月壬戌，帝至彭城，解嚴息甲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, on the day renxu, the Emperor reached Pengcheng, lifted martial readiness, and rested the armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, on the day renxu, the Emperor reached Pengcheng and stood the army down.

sentences.zh: 以輔國將軍劉遵考為并州刺史，領河東太守，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Assistant General Who Assists the State Liu Zunkao was made Governor of Bing and concurrently Governor of Hedong, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao, Assistant General Who Assists the State, was made Governor of Bing and Hedong and garrisoned Puban.

sentences.zh: 帝解司州，領徐、冀二州刺史，固讓進爵。

translations.literal: The Emperor relinquished Si province and took Xu and Ji; he firmly declined advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave up Si province and took Xu and Ji, but again refused advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 時漢中成固縣漢水崖際有異聲如雷，俄頃岸崩，有銅鍾十二，出自潛壤。

translations.literal: At that time on the cliff edge of the Han River at Chenggu county in Hanzhong there was a strange sound like thunder; in a moment the bank collapsed, and twelve bronze bells emerged from the hidden earth.
translations.idiomatic: At that time on the Han River cliffs at Chenggu in Hanzhong came a sound like thunder. The bank collapsed, and twelve bronze bells rose from the buried earth.

sentences.zh: 鞏縣人宗曜于其田所獲嘉禾，九穗同莖，帝以獻，晉帝以歸於我。

translations.literal: Zong Yao, a man of Gong county, obtained fine grain in his field—nine ears on one stem; the Emperor offered it; the Jin emperor returned it to us.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yao of Gong county found fine grain in his field, nine ears on a single stalk. The Emperor sent it as tribute, and the Jin emperor returned it to him.

sentences.zh: 帝沖讓，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor modestly declined, and then it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor modestly declined, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 六月丁亥，受相國宋公九錫之命，下命赦國內殊死以下。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai in the sixth month he received the mandate of Chief Minister Duke of Song and the nine bestowals; he issued orders pardoning within the state all guilty of special death and below.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai in the sixth month he received the mandate of Chief Minister, Duke of Song, and the Nine Bestowals, and ordered a pardon for all within the state guilty of capital crimes and below.

sentences.zh: 詔崇豫章太夫人為宋公太妃，世子為中軍將軍副貳，相國府百官悉依天朝之制。

translations.literal: An edict honored the Grand Matron of Yuzhang as Grand Consort of the Duke of Song; the heir as Central Army General and deputy; all hundred offices of the Chief Minister's headquarters all followed the heavenly court's system.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made the Grand Matron of Yuzhang Grand Consort of the Duke of Song and the heir Central Army General and deputy at the Chief Minister's headquarters; all other offices followed the imperial court's system.

sentences.zh: 又詔宋國所封十郡之外，悉得除用。

translations.literal: Again it was ordered that beyond the ten commanderies enfeoffed to the state of Song, all might be appointed and employed.
translations.idiomatic: It was also ordered that appointments might be made beyond the ten commanderies of Song.

sentences.zh: 先是，安西中兵參軍沈田子殺安西司馬王鎮惡，諸將殺安西長史王修，關中亂。

translations.literal: Earlier Pacifying-the-West Central Army Adviser Shen Tianzi killed Pacifying-the-West Marshal Wang Zhen'e; the generals killed Pacifying-the-West Chief of Staff Wang Xiu; Guanzhong was in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shen Tianzi, staff officer of the Pacifying West army, killed Wang Zhen'e, its marshal; the generals then killed Wang Xiu, its chief of staff. Guanzhong fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝遣右將軍朱齡石代安西將軍桂陽公義真為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Right General Zhu Lingshi to replace Pacifying-the-West General Duke of Guiyang Yizhen as Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Zhu Lingshi, Right General, to replace Yizhen as Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 義真還，為赫連勃勃所追，大敗，僅以身免，諸將帥及齡石並沒。

translations.literal: When Yizhen had returned, he was pursued by Helian Bobo, greatly defeated, and barely escaped with his person; the generals and commanders and Lingshi were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yizhen was pursued by Helian Bobo, routed, and barely escaped alive. The generals and Lingshi were all lost.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉安帝崩，大司馬琅邪王即帝位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Emperor An of Jin died; the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, took the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Emperor An of Jin died. The Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年正月，晉帝詔征帝入輔，又申前令，進公爵為王，以徐州之海陵北東海北譙北梁、豫州之新蔡、兗州之北陳留、司州之陳郡汝南潁川滎陽十郡，增宋國。
