translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanxi the Jin emperor ordered the Emperor summoned to assist at court, again pressed the earlier command, advanced the Duke to King, and with the ten commanderies of Hailing, Northern Donghai, Northern Qiao, and Northern Liang in Xuzhou, Xincai in Yuzhou, Northern Chenliu in Yanzhou, and Chen, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xingyang in Sizhou, increased the state of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yuanxi the Jin emperor summoned the Emperor to court, again pressed the earlier honors on him, advanced the Duke to King, and added ten commanderies to Song: Hailing, Northern Donghai, Northern Qiao, and Northern Liang in Xuzhou; Xincai in Yuzhou; Northern Chenliu in Yanzhou; and Chen, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xingyang in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，乃受命。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he then accepted the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he at last accepted the mandate.

sentences.zh: 赦國內五歲刑以下，遷都壽陽。

translations.literal: He pardoned within the state all guilty of five-year punishments and below; he moved the capital to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned all within the state guilty of punishments of five years and below and moved the capital to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，解揚州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he relinquished Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he relinquished Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉帝命帝冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鍾虡宮縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Jin emperor ordered the Emperor's cap with twelve tassels, established the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, going out with police and entering with imperial escort, riding the golden-root chariot, driving six horses, provided with five-season secondary chariots, setting yak-tail and cloud pennants, music and dance of eight rows, and setting bells and suspended stones in palace arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Jin emperor granted him the twelve-tassel cap, the Son of Heaven's banners, imperial escort, the golden-root chariot with six horses, five seasonal chariots, yak-tail and cloud pennants, eight-row dance, and palace bells.

sentences.zh: 進王太妃為太后，王妃為王后，世子為太子，王子、王孫爵命之號，一如舊儀。

translations.literal: The king's grand consort was advanced to Empress Dowager; the king's consort to Queen; the heir to Crown Prince; the titles of prince and king's grandson—all like the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was made Empress Dowager, his wife Queen, his heir Crown Prince; titles for princes and grandsons followed the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，帝表讓殊禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the Emperor submitted a memorial declining the special honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the Emperor memorialized declining these special honors.

sentences.zh: 竟陵郡江濱自開，出古銅禮器十餘枚，帝獻之晉帝，讓不受，於是歸諸瑞物，藏於相府。

translations.literal: At the Jiang riverbank in Jingling commandery the ground opened by itself; more than ten ancient bronze ritual vessels emerged; the Emperor offered them to the Jin emperor, who declined and did not accept; thereupon they were returned to the auspicious objects and stored at the Chief Minister's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiang riverbank in Jingling commandery the ground opened by itself, and more than ten ancient bronze ritual vessels emerged. The Emperor offered them to the Jin emperor, who declined to accept them; they were then treated as auspicious objects and stored at the Chief Minister's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔遣敦勸，兼征帝入輔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict sent earnest persuasion and also summoned the Emperor to assist at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict sent earnest persuasion and again summoned the Emperor to court.

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，帝至都。

translations.literal: On the day renxu in the sixth month the Emperor reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu in the sixth month the Emperor reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，晉帝禪位於宋。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin the Jin emperor abdicated the throne to Song.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin the Jin emperor abdicated to Song.

sentences.zh: 有司草詔既成，請書之，天子即便操筆，謂左右曰：「桓玄之時，天命已改，重為劉公所延，將二十載。

translations.literal: When the draft edict was complete it was sent and presented to the Son of Heaven to have him write it; the Son of Heaven then at once took up the brush and said to those at his side: "In the time of Huan Xuan Heaven's mandate had already changed; I was again extended by Duke Liu for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication edict was drafted, it was sent to the emperor to copy. He took the brush at once and said to those beside him: "Under Huan Xuan the mandate had already changed. Duke Liu extended my reign for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，本所甘心。

translations.literal: Today's affair is originally what my heart is willing for.
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair is what my heart has long accepted.

sentences.zh: 」甲子，遣使奉策曰：

translations.literal: " On the day jiazi he sent envoys bearing the mandate document, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " On the day jiazi he sent envoys bearing the mandate document, which read:

sentences.zh: 咨爾宋王，夫玄古權輿，悠哉邈矣，其詳靡得而聞。

translations.literal: Consult you, King of Song: the dark antiquity when power first arose—how far and remote! Its details cannot be heard.
translations.idiomatic: To you, King of Song: in deepest antiquity, when rule first arose, the details are lost in time.

sentences.zh: 爰自書契，降逮三、五，莫不以上聖君四海，止戈定大業。

translations.literal: From when writing and tallies descended down to the Three and Five, none did not use the highest sage to lord the four seas, stop weapons and fix the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of writing down to the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, sages ruled the four seas, stopped war, and fixed the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 然則帝王者，宰物之通器，君道者，天下之至公也。

translations.literal: Thus the emperor and king is the common vessel for ruling things; the Way of the ruler is the utmost fairness under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is the vessel for ruling all things; the ruler's way is the utmost fairness under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔在上葉，深鑒茲道，是以天祿既終，唐、虞弗得傳其嗣，符命來格，舜、禹不獲全其謙。

translations.literal: In former days in the upper age, deeply reflecting on this Way, therefore when Heaven's blessing had ended, Tang and Yu could not transmit their heirs; when the mandate's talisman came, Shun and Yu could not preserve their modesty whole.
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity, when Heaven's blessing ended, Tang and Yu could not pass the throne to their sons; when the mandate came, Shun and Yu could not keep their modest refusal.

sentences.zh: 所以經緯三才，澄序彝化，作范振古，垂風萬葉，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: Therefore to weave the three powers, clarify and order the transforming norms, make a model to shake antiquity, and hand down wind for ten thousand generations—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they ordered the three realms, set the transforming norms, made models for all time, and handed down virtue for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 自是厥後，歷代彌劭。

translations.literal: From this thereafter, generation after generation grew more emphatic.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each age grew stronger in this.

sentences.zh: 漢既嗣德於放勳，魏亦方軌于重華，諒以協謀乎人鬼，而以百姓為心者也。

translations.literal: Han continued the virtue of Emperor Yao; Wei also squared the track of Chonghua—truly they coordinated plans between men and ghosts, and took the hundred surnames as heart.
translations.idiomatic: Han followed Yao's virtue; Wei matched Shun's track. They harmonized men and spirits and took the people as their heart.

sentences.zh: 昔我祖宗欽明，辰居其極，而明晦代序，盈虧有期，翦商兆禍，非惟一世，曾是弗克，矧伊在今，天之所廢，有自來矣。

translations.literal: In former days our ancestors were reverent and bright; the Star dwelt at the pole; yet bright and dark succeeded in order; fullness and deficit had their terms; the omen of cutting Shang brought calamity—not for one age alone; once this could not be overcome—how much more in the present! What Heaven abolishes has come from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors were reverent and bright, and the pole star stood firm; yet light and dark alternate, and fullness and waning have their terms. The fall of Shang foretold calamity for many ages. Once it could not be overcome; how much less today. What Heaven abolishes has long been foretold.

sentences.zh: 惟王體上聖之姿，包二儀之德，明齊日月，道合四時。

translations.literal: Only the king's person holds the posture of the highest sage, embraces the virtue of the two regulators, brightness equal to sun and moon, Way matching the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Only you hold the sage's stature, embrace heaven and earth's virtue, shine like sun and moon, and match the four seasons in your Way.

sentences.zh: 乃者，社稷傾覆，王拯而存之，中原蕪梗，又濟而復之。

translations.literal: Then the altars of state toppled and overturned—the king rescued and preserved them; the central plains were wasteland and blocked—again he crossed and restored them.
translations.idiomatic: When the altars fell, you saved them; when the central plains lay waste, you restored them.

sentences.zh: 自負固不賓，幹紀放命，肆逆滔天，竊據萬里，靡不潤之以風雨，震之以雷霆。

translations.literal: From those who relied on solidity and would not guest, to those who violated discipline and threw off mandate, running riot and flooding Heaven, stealing and occupying ten thousand li—none were not moistened with wind and rain, shaken with thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: From stubborn rebels to those who defied the law and seized vast territories—none escaped your rain of grace or thunder of wrath.

sentences.zh: 九伐之道既敷，八法之化自理，豈伊博施於人，濟斯黔庶，固已義洽四海，道盛八荒者矣。

translations.literal: The Way of the nine campaigns was already spread; the transformation of the eight methods was naturally ordered—how could it be only spreading broadly among the people and crossing this black-headed multitude; firmly righteousness has harmonized the four seas; the Way's flourishing fills the eight regions.
translations.idiomatic: The nine campaigns were carried out; the eight methods brought order. You have not only enriched the people and saved the masses; your righteousness fills the four seas and your authority the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 至於上天垂象，四靈效征，圖讖之文既明，人神之望已改，百工歌于朝，庶人頌乎野，億兆抃踴，傾佇惟新。

translations.literal: As for Heaven above hanging images, the four numina effecting omens, the texts of charts and prophecies already clarified, the hope of men and spirits already changed—the hundred craftsmen sing in the court; the many people chant in the wild; the hundred millions stamp and leap; leaning and waiting, they look only for the new.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shows signs; the four spirits send omens; prophecies are clear; men and spirits have turned their hope. Craftsmen sing in court, people chant in the fields, and all the realm leaps, awaiting the new age.

sentences.zh: 自非百姓樂推，天命攸集，豈伊在予所得獨專。

translations.literal: Unless the hundred surnames joyfully pushed and Heaven's mandate thereby gathered—how could it be in me alone that what was obtained was exclusively held?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the people pushed and Heaven's mandate gathered, how could I hold this alone?

sentences.zh: 是用仰祗皇靈，俯順群議，敬禪神器，授帝位於爾躬。

translations.literal: Therefore I respectfully look up to the imperial numen and bow to follow the counsel of the masses, respectfully abdicating the divine vessel and conferring the emperor's position on your person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I reverently follow Heaven and the people's will, abdicate the throne, and confer the imperial seat upon you.

sentences.zh: 大祚其窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: The great fortune is exhausted; Heaven's blessing forever ends.
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune is ended; Heaven's blessing passes away.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 王其允執其中，敬遵典訓，副率土之嘉願，恢洪業于無窮，時膺休佑，以答三靈之眷望。

translations.literal: King, you must truly hold the center, respectfully follow the canon and instructions, assist the excellent wish of all within the lands, restore the great enterprise without end, timely receive fine blessing, to answer the three spirits' look of attachment.
translations.idiomatic: King, hold the center, follow the canon, fulfill the realm's wish, extend the great enterprise without end, receive Heaven's blessing, and answer the three spirits' regard.

sentences.zh: 又遣使持節、兼太保、散騎常侍、光祿大夫謝澹，兼太尉、尚書劉宣范奉璽書，歸皇帝璽綬，受終之禮，一如唐虞、漢魏故事。

translations.literal: Again he sent Commissioner with credentials, concurrently Grand Tutor, Regular Attendant, Household Master of Light Xie Tan, concurrently Grand Commandant, Master of Writing Liu Xuanfan, bearing the imperial letter, returning the imperial seals and cord, with the rites of receiving the end—all like the stories of Tang-Yu and Han-Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Commissioner Xie Tan, Grand Tutor and Household Master of Light, and Liu Xuanfan, Grand Commandant and Master of Writing, bearing the imperial letter, returning the imperial seals and cord, with the rites of abdication following the precedents of Tang-Yu and Han-Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝奉表陳讓，晉帝已遜于琅邪王第，表不獲通。

translations.literal: The Emperor submitted a memorial declining; the Jin emperor had already yielded to the Prince of Langye's residence; the memorial could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor submitted a memorial of refusal. The Jin emperor had already moved to the Prince of Langye's residence; the memorial could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 於是陳留王虔嗣等二百七十人及宋台群臣並上表勸進，猶不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Chenliu Qian Si and two hundred seventy others, and the multitude of ministers of the Song headquarters, all submitted memorials urging advancement—and he still did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qian Si, Prince of Chenliu, with two hundred seventy others, and all the ministers of Song, memorialized urging him to accept the throne. He still refused.

sentences.zh: 太史令駱達陳天文符應曰：「案晉義熙元年至元熙元年，太白晝見經天凡七，占曰：'太白經天，人更主，異姓興。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Luo Da presented the correspondence of astronomical signs, saying: "Examining from the first year of Yixi of Jin to the first year of Yuanxi, Venus was seen in daylight crossing the heavens seven times in all; the prognostication says: 'Venus crossing the heavens—rulers change, a different surname rises.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Luo Da presented the correspondence of heavenly signs, saying: "From the first year of Yixi of Jin to the first year of Yuanxi, Venus crossed the heavens in daylight seven times. The prognostication says: 'When Venus crosses the heavens, rulers change and a different surname rises.

sentences.zh: '義熙七年，五虹見於東方，占曰：'五虹見，天子黜，聖人出。

translations.literal: ' In the seventh year of Yixi, five rainbows appeared in the east; the prognostication says: 'Five rainbows appear—the Son of Heaven is deposed, a sage emerges.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the seventh year of Yixi, five rainbows appeared in the east. The prognostication says: 'When five rainbows appear, the Son of Heaven is deposed and a sage emerges.

sentences.zh: '九年，鎮星、歲星、太白、熒惑聚于東井。

translations.literal: ' In the ninth year, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, and Mars gathered in the Well.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the ninth year, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, and Mars gathered in the Well constellation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，鎮星入太微。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Saturn entered the Grand Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Saturn entered the Grand Subtlety.

sentences.zh: 占曰：'鎮星守太微，有立王，有徙王。

translations.literal: The prognostication says: 'Saturn guarding the Grand Subtlety—a king is established, a king is displaced.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication says: 'When Saturn guards the Grand Subtlety, a king is established and a king is displaced.

sentences.zh: '元熙元年冬，黑龍四登于天，易傳曰：'冬，龍見，天子亡社稷，大人受命。

translations.literal: ' In the winter of the first year of Yuanxi, black dragons ascended to heaven four times; the Commentary on the Changes says: 'In winter, a dragon appears—the Son of Heaven loses the altars of state; a great man receives the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the winter of the first year of Yuanxi, black dragons ascended to heaven four times. The Commentary on the Changes says: 'When a dragon appears in winter, the Son of Heaven loses the altars of state and a great man receives the mandate.

sentences.zh: '冀州道人釋法稱告其弟子曰：'嵩神言，江東有劉將軍，漢家苗裔，當受天命，吾以璧三十二、鎮金一餅與之，劉氏卜世之數也。

translations.literal: ' The Daoist monk Fazheng of Jizhou told his disciples: 'The Spirit of Mount Song says: In the lands east of the river there is General Liu, a scion of the Han house, who is to receive Heaven's mandate; I give him thirty-two jade disks and one ingot of stabilizing gold—the number by which the Liu house's reign is divined.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Daoist monk Fazheng of Jizhou told his disciples: 'The Spirit of Mount Song says: East of the river there is General Liu, a scion of the Han house, who is to receive Heaven's mandate. I give him thirty-two jade disks and one ingot of stabilizing gold—the number by which the Liu house's reign is divined.

sentences.zh: '漢建武至建安末一百九十六年而禪魏，魏自黃初至咸熙末四十六年而禪晉，晉自泰始至今百五十六年，三代揖讓，咸窮於六。

translations.literal: ' From Jianwu of Han to the end of Jian'an, one hundred ninety-six years, then abdication to Wei; from Huangchu of Wei to the end of Xianxi, forty-six years, then abdication to Jin; from Taishi of Jin to the present, one hundred fifty-six years—three dynasties yielding the throne, all exhausted at six.
translations.idiomatic: ' From Jianwu of Han to the end of Jian'an was one hundred ninety-six years, then abdication to Wei; from Huangchu of Wei to the end of Xianxi was forty-six years, then abdication to Jin; from Taishi of Jin to the present is one hundred fifty-six years. Three dynasties yielding the throne all exhausted their term at six.

sentences.zh: 又漢光武社於南陽，漢末而其樹死，劉備有蜀，乃應之而興；

translations.literal: Also when Emperor Guangwu of Han established the altars at Nanyang, the tree there died at the end of Han; when Liu Bei had Shu, it responded and flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Also when Emperor Guangwu of Han established the altars at Nanyang, the tree there died at the end of Han; when Liu Bei held Shu, it responded and flourished;

sentences.zh: 及晉季年，舊根始萌，至是而盛矣。

translations.literal: by the last years of Jin the old root first sprouted, and by now it had grown luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: by the last years of Jin the old root first sprouted, and by now it had grown luxuriant.

sentences.zh: 」若此者有數十條。

translations.literal: There were several tens of items like these.
translations.idiomatic: There were several tens of items like these.

sentences.zh: 群臣又固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: The multitude of ministers again firmly requested—and he then followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed again, and he at last accepted.

sentences.zh: 永初元年夏六月丁卯，皇帝即位于南郊，設壇，柴燎告天曰：

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on the day dingmao of the first year of Yongchu, the Emperor took the imperial position at the southern suburb, set up an altar, burned firewood to announce to Heaven, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of the inaugural year Yongchu, on the day dingmao, the Emperor took the throne at the southern suburb, raised an altar, burned firewood to announce his accession to Heaven, and said:

sentences.zh: 皇帝臣裕敢用玄牡，昭告於皇皇后帝：

translations.literal: The Emperor, your subject Yu, ventures to use a black bull, proclaiming clearly to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, your subject Yu, ventures to offer a black bull and proclaim plainly to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth:

sentences.zh: 晉以卜世告終，歷數有歸，欽若景運，以命於裕。

translations.literal: The Jin Emperor, because divination showed his dynasty's allotted span had ended and the mandate had found its destination, reverently followed the flourishing fortune and entrusted the mandate to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor, because divination showed his dynasty's term had ended and the mandate had passed to its rightful holder, reverently followed the age's flourishing fortune and entrusted the mandate to Yu.

sentences.zh: 夫樹君宰世，天下為公，德充帝王，樂推攸集。

translations.literal: To establish a ruler and govern the age—under Heaven all is public; when virtue fills the place of emperor or king, willing abdication gathers of itself.
translations.idiomatic: To set up a ruler and govern the world: the realm belongs to all; when virtue matches that of emperors and kings, the people's willing endorsement gathers of itself.

sentences.zh: 越俶唐虞，降暨漢魏，靡不以上哲格文祖，元勳陟帝位，故能大拯黔首，垂訓無窮。

translations.literal: Tracing from Yao and Shun down through Han and Wei, none failed to have a supreme sage align with the culture-founding ancestor and a chief merit-holder ascend the imperial seat, thereby able greatly to rescue the black-headed people and hand down instruction without end.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao and Shun down through Han and Wei, none failed to have a supreme sage align with the founding ancestor of civilization and a chief merit-holder ascend the throne, thereby greatly rescuing the common people and handing down instruction without end.

sentences.zh: 晉自東遷，四維不振，宰輔焉依，為日已久。

translations.literal: Since the Jin moved east, the four bonds were not secured; reliance on chief ministers had already lasted a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin moved south, the four pillars of order no longer held firm, and the court had long depended on chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 難棘隆安，禍成元興，遂至帝主遷播，宗祀堙滅。

translations.literal: Distress piled up in the Long'an reign, disaster took shape in the Yuanxing era, until sovereigns were driven to wander and ancestral sacrifices were buried and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Hardship piled up in the Long'an era, catastrophe took shape under Yuanxing, until emperors were driven from the capital and the ancestral rites were cut off.

sentences.zh: 裕雖地非齊、晉，眾無一旅，仰憤時難，俯悼橫流，投袂一起，則皇祀克復。

translations.literal: Though Yu's territory was not like Qi or Jin and his forces lacked a full regiment, looking up he was stirred by the age's hardship, looking down he grieved the flood of ruin; with a shake of his sleeve and one command, the imperial sacrifices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yu's domain was no match for Qi or Jin and his forces scarcely amounted to a regiment, he looked up in anger at the age's calamities and down in grief at the flood of ruin; with a shake of his sleeve and one command, the imperial sacrifices were restored.

sentences.zh: 及危而能持，顛而能扶，奸宄具殲，僭偽亦滅，誠興廢有期，否終有數。

translations.literal: In danger he could hold fast; when overturned he could set upright; treacherous evildoers were entirely exterminated; usurping pretenders were also destroyed—truly, revival of what was abolished has its season; the end of obstruction has its count.
translations.idiomatic: In peril he could hold firm; when the order was overturned he could set it right; treacherous evildoers were wiped out and usurping pretenders destroyed. Truly, the revival of what had been cast down has its season, and the end of decline has its reckoning.

sentences.zh: 至於大造晉室，撥亂濟時，因藉時來，實屍其重。

translations.literal: As to greatly rebuilding the Jin house, putting down disorder and aiding the age—riding the tide of the times, he truly bore its weight.
translations.idiomatic: As for greatly rebuilding the Jin house, quelling chaos and succoring the age—riding the tide of the times, he truly bore the heaviest burden.

sentences.zh: 加以殊俗慕義，重譯來庭，正朔所暨，咸服聲教。

translations.literal: Moreover, distant peoples admired righteousness; repeated translators came to court; wherever the correct calendar reached, all submitted to transforming instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, distant peoples admired righteousness, envoys came again and again to court, and wherever the imperial calendar reached, all submitted to civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 至乃三靈垂象，山川告祥，人神協祉，歲月滋著。

translations.literal: Even the three luminous bodies sent down signs, mountains and rivers announced auspice, man and spirits joined in blessing—the months and years daily grew manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Even the three luminaries sent down portents, mountains and rivers announced auspicious signs, and heaven and earth joined in blessing, so that the mandate grew clearer month by month and year by year.

sentences.zh: 是以群公卿士，億兆夷人，僉曰：「皇靈降鑒於上，晉朝款誠於下，天命不可以久淹，宸極不可以暫曠。

translations.literal: Therefore dukes, ministers, and officials, the hundred million common folk, all said the August Spirit sent down inspection from above, the Jin court showed sincerity below—the Mandate of Heaven cannot long be delayed, the imperial pinnacle cannot briefly be vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the nobles, ministers, and officials, and the hundred million common people, all said that the August Spirit looked down from above while the Jin court showed sincerity below: the Mandate of Heaven could not long be delayed, and the imperial throne could not remain vacant.

sentences.zh: 」遂逼群議，恭茲大禮。

translations.literal: They thereupon pressed him with collective counsel and respectfully performed this great rite.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon pressed him with collective counsel and respectfully performed this great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 猥以寡德，托於兆人之上，雖仰畏天威，略是小節，顧深永懷，祗懼若霣。

translations.literal: Humbly with scant virtue, resting on the myriad people above—though in awe of Heaven's majesty this is a small ceremony, yet turning deeply to lasting recollection, reverent fear as though falling.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly, with scant virtue, I rest upon the myriad people above; though in awe of Heaven's majesty this is a small matter, yet turning deeply to lasting recollection, I am reverently fearful as though about to fall.

sentences.zh: 敬簡元日，升壇受禪，告類上帝，用酬萬國之情，克隆天保，永祚于有宋。

translations.literal: Respectfully selecting the great day, ascending the altar to receive the abdication, announcing the category to High God, thereby answering all under Heaven's feeling, may Heaven's blessing be magnified, and everlasting fortune rest on Song.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully selecting this great day, I ascend the altar to receive the abdication, announce the succession to High God, answer the feeling of all under Heaven, magnify Heaven's blessing, and grant everlasting fortune to Song.

sentences.zh: 惟明靈是饗！

translations.literal: May the luminous spirits be satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: May the luminous spirits accept this offering!

sentences.zh: 禮畢，備法駕，幸建康宮，臨太極前殿，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: When the rite was concluded, with full imperial equipage he proceeded to Jiankang Palace, attended the front hall of the Grand Ultimate, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was concluded, with full imperial equipage he went to Jiankang Palace, took his seat in the front hall of the Grand Ultimate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 賜人爵二級。

translations.literal: He granted the people two ranks of noble status.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the people two ranks of noble status.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，人穀五斛，逋租宿責勿收。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who could not support themselves—each person was given five piculs of grain; overdue rents and old debts were not collected.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute who could not support themselves received five piculs of grain each; overdue rents and old debts were not collected.

sentences.zh: 其犯鄉論清議，贓汙淫盜，一皆蕩滌。

translations.literal: Those who violated village discourse and pure judgment, or committed corruption, debauchery, or theft—all were entirely cleared and washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Those who violated village standards of conduct, or committed corruption, debauchery, or theft—all were cleared entirely.

sentences.zh: 長徒之身，特皆原遣。

translations.literal: Persons sentenced to long penal service were especially all pardoned and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Persons sentenced to long penal service were all specially pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 亡官失爵、禁錮奪勞，一依舊准。

translations.literal: Those who lost office or rank, were forbidden from office, or had labor levies taken—all followed the old standards.
translations.idiomatic: Those who lost office or rank, were barred from office, or had labor levies taken—all followed the former standards.

sentences.zh: 封晉帝為零陵王，全食一郡，載天子旌旗，乘五時副車，行晉正朔，郊祀天地，禮樂制度，皆用晉典，上書不為表，答表不稱詔，宮於故秣陵。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Lingling, with the full revenue of one commandery, bearing the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, riding the five-season secondary chariot, following the Jin calendar, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth with Jin rites, music, and institutions; in memorials to the throne he did not use the form "memorial"; in replies to memorials the word "edict" was not used; he was housed at the old Moling.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Lingling, with the full revenue of one commandery. He bore the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, rode the five-season secondary chariot, followed the Jin calendar, and in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, rites, music, and institutions—all followed Jin regulations. In memorials to the throne he did not use the form "memorial"; in replies the word "edict" was not used. He was housed at the old Moling.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇考為孝穆皇帝，妣為穆皇后，尊王太后為皇太后。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored his late father as Emperor Xiaomu, his late mother as Empress Mu, and honored the Wang Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his late father as Emperor Xiaomu, his late mother as Empress Mu, and honored the Wang Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫微禹之感，歎深後昆，愛人懷樹，猶或勿翦。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The feeling at Wei's slighting of Yu runs deep for later generations; one who loves others cherishes their trees, and even then may not cut them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The regret at slighting Yu runs deep for later generations; one who loves others cherishes their trees, and even then may not cut them.

sentences.zh: 雖在異代，義無廢絕，降殺之儀，一依前典。

translations.literal: Though in a different age, righteousness does not permit extinction; the propriety of lowering and reducing ranks should wholly follow the former canon.
translations.idiomatic: Though in a different age, righteousness does not permit extinction; the propriety of lowering ranks should wholly follow the former canon.

sentences.zh: 可降始興公為縣公，廬陵公為柴桑縣公，始安公為荔浦縣侯，長沙公為醴陵縣侯，康樂公即降為縣侯，奉王導、謝安、溫嶠、陶侃、謝玄之祀，其宣力義熙者，一仍本秩。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Shixing may be reduced to Duke of Shixing county, the Duke of Luling to Duke of Chaisang county, the Duke of Shi'an to Marquis of Lipu, the Duke of Changsha to Marquis of Liling; the Duke of Kangle is immediately reduced to county marquis—to maintain the sacrifices to Wang Dao, Xie An, Wen Qiao, Tao Kan, and Xie Xuan. Those who exerted strength in the Yixi era keep their original ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Shixing may be reduced to Duke of Shixing county, the Duke of Luling to Duke of Chaisang county, the Duke of Shi'an to Marquis of Lipu, the Duke of Changsha to Marquis of Liling; the Duke of Kangle is immediately reduced to county marquis—to maintain the sacrifices to Wang Dao, Xie An, Wen Qiao, Tao Kan, and Xie Xuan. Those who exerted strength in the Yixi era keep their original ranks."

sentences.zh: 庚午，以司空道憐為太尉，封長沙王，立南郡公義慶為臨川王。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the Minister of Works Dao Lin was made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha; Duke of Nan Commandery Yiqing was established as Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, Dao Lin, Minister of Works, was made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha; Yiqing, Duke of Nan Commandery, was established as Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 又詔論戰亡追贈及酬賞除復之科。

translations.literal: Again an edict set forth the categories for posthumous compensation of those who died in battle and for reward, compensation, and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also set forth regulations for posthumous compensation and rewards for those who died in battle.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，封皇子桂陽公義真為廬陵王，彭城公義隆為宜都王，義康為彭城王。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was established as Prince of Luling; Duke of Pengcheng Yilong as Prince of Yidu; Yikang as Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Yizhen, Duke of Guiyang, was established as Prince of Luling; Yilong, Duke of Pengcheng, as Prince of Yidu; Yikang as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，使使巡行四方，旌賢舉善，問人疾苦，獄訟虧濫、政刑乖愆、傷化擾俗、未允人聽者，皆具以聞。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, envoys were sent to travel the four directions, displaying the worthy and raising the good, asking of the people's afflictions; where lawsuits were deficient or excessive, government and punishments deviated, harm to transformation and disturbance of custom failed to satisfy the people's hearing—all were to report fully.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, envoys were sent to travel the four directions, displaying the worthy and raising the good and asking of the people's afflictions. Where lawsuits were deficient or excessive, government and punishments deviated, or harm to order and disturbance of custom failed to satisfy the people's hearing—all were to report fully.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔增百官奉。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, an edict increased the salaries of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin, an edict increased the salaries of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 己卯，改晉泰始曆為永初曆，社以子，臘以辰。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the Jin Taishi calendar was changed to the Yongchu calendar; the communal sacrifice at the zi day, the winter sacrifice at the chen day.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, the Jin Taishi calendar was changed to the Yongchu calendar, with the communal sacrifice at the zi day and the winter sacrifice at the chen day.

sentences.zh: 八月辛酉，詔舊郡縣以北為名者悉除之，寓立于南者，聽以南為號。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou in the eighth month, an edict ordered that all old commanderies and counties that used "north" in their names remove it; those established in the south as exiles might use "south" in their designation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou in the eighth month, an edict ordered that all old commanderies and counties with "north" in their names remove it; those established in the south as exiles might use "south" in their designation.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔曰：「彭城桑梓，敦本斯隆，宜同豐、沛。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, an edict stated: "Pengcheng is the mulberry-and-catalpa homeland; honoring one's roots should be exalted—as with Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen, an edict stated: "Pengcheng is the mulberry-and-catalpa homeland; honoring one's roots should be exalted—as with Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 其沛郡、下邳各復租布三十年。

translations.literal: Pei commandery and Xiapi may each have land cloth exempted for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Pei commandery and Xiapi may each have land cloth exempted for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 」辛未，追諡妃臧氏為敬皇后，陵曰永寧。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the late consort Lady Zang was posthumously titled Empress Jing; the tomb was named Everlasting Peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, the late consort Lady Zang was posthumously titled Empress Jing; her tomb was named Everlasting Peace.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，立王太子義符為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Wang heir apparent Yifu was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, the crown prince Yifu was established as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，赦見罪人。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, those currently under punishment were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, those currently under punishment were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬午，置晉帝諸陵守衛，其名賢先哲，詳加灑掃。

translations.literal: On the day renwu in the intercalary month, guards were established for the tombs of the Jin emperors; famous worthies and former sages were carefully swept and sprinkled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu in the intercalary month, guards were established for the tombs of the Jin emperors; famous worthies and former sages were carefully swept and tended.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，林邑國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Lin Yi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Lin Yi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 九月壬子，置東宮殿中將軍十人，員外二十人。

translations.literal: On the day renzi in the ninth month, ten Eastern Palace Palace Army commanders and twenty supernumerary posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth month, on the day renzi, ten Eastern Palace Palace Army commanders were established, with twenty supernumerary posts.

sentences.zh: 壬申，置都官尚書。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the Minister of Justice was established.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, the post of Minister of Justice was established.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏明元皇帝泰常五年。

translations.literal: This year was the fifth year of Taichang of Emperor Mingyuan of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the fifth year of Taichang under Emperor Mingyuan of Wei.

sentences.zh: 西涼亡。

translations.literal: Western Liang perished.
translations.idiomatic: Western Liang fell.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛酉，祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In the second year, in the first month on the day xinyou, he sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the day xinyou in the first month, he sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，斷金銀塗。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, gilt with gold and silver was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin, the use of gold and silver gilding was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 以揚州刺史廬陵王義真為司徒，以尚書僕射徐羨之為尚書令、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Yizhen, Prince of Luling and Governor of Yangzhou, was made Grand Tutor; Xu Xianzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen, Prince of Luling and Governor of Yangzhou, was made Grand Tutor. Xu Xianzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，禁喪事用銅釘。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the use of copper nails in funerals was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, copper nails were forbidden in funerals.

sentences.zh: 罷會稽郡府。

translations.literal: The commandery headquarters of Kuaiji was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji commandery headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二月己丑，策試州郡秀、孝於延賢堂。

translations.literal: In the second month on the day jichou, provincial and commandery candidates for Flowering Talent and Filial Piety were examined by decree at the Hall of Extended Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jichou, provincial and commandery candidates for the Flowering Talent and Filial Piety titles were examined by decree in the Hall of Extended Worthies.

sentences.zh: 倭國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Wa sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wa sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，初限荊州府置將不得過二千人，吏不得過一萬人。

translations.literal: In the third month on the day yichou, a limit was first set: Jing province headquarters might not have more than two thousand officers, nor more than ten thousand clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day yichou, limits were first imposed: Jing province headquarters could have no more than two thousand officers and ten thousand clerks.

sentences.zh: 州置將不得過五百人，吏不得過五千人。

translations.literal: For commandery headquarters, officers might not exceed five hundred, clerks five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: For commandery headquarters, officers were capped at five hundred and clerks at five thousand.

sentences.zh: 兵士不在此限。

translations.literal: Soldiers were not subject to this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were exempt from these limits.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己卯，初禁淫祀，除諸房廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on the day jimao, illicit shrines were first forbidden, and the various lineage temples were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jimao, illicit shrines were first forbidden and private lineage temples were abolished.

sentences.zh: 其先賢以勳德立祠者，不在此例。

translations.literal: Those for whom former worthies had established shrines for merit and virtue were not included in this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines erected to former worthies for merit and virtue were exempt.

sentences.zh: 戊申，聽訟于華林園。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, he heard lawsuits at Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen, he heard lawsuits in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 五月己酉，置東宮屯騎、步兵、翊軍三校尉官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on the day jiyou, three corps commanders were established for the Eastern Palace: Mounted, Foot, and Assisting Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jiyou, three Eastern Palace corps commanders were established: Mounted, Foot, and Assisting Army.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己巳，地震。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on the day jisi, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jisi, the earth quaked.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，零陵王殂，宋志也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on the day jichou, the Prince of Lingling died—this is in the Song Annals.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, the Prince of Lingling died—as recorded in the Song Annals.

sentences.zh: 車駕率百僚臨於朝堂三日，如魏明帝服山陽公故事。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage with the hundred officials attended at the court hall for three days, following Emperor Ming of Wei's mourning for the Duke of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor with the hundred officials attended at the court hall for three days, following Emperor Ming of Wei's precedent in mourning the Duke of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 使兼太尉持節護喪事，葬以晉禮。

translations.literal: He sent the concurrent Grand Commandant with credentials to oversee the funeral, and burial followed Jin rites.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the concurrent Grand Commandant with credentials to oversee the funeral; burial followed Jin rites.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己亥，以涼州胡帥大沮渠蒙遜為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on the day jihai, Juqu Mengxun, Xiongnu chieftain of Liang province, was made Grand General Who Guards the Army, with the privileges of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jihai, Juqu Mengxun, Xiongnu chieftain of Liang province, was made Grand General Who Guards the Army, granted privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛亥，葬晉恭皇帝于沖平陵，車駕率百官瞻送。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on the day xinhai, Emperor Gong of Jin was buried at Chongping Mausoleum; the imperial carriage with the hundred officials witnessed the funeral procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day xinhai, Emperor Gong of Jin was buried at Chongping Mausoleum; the Emperor with the hundred officials attended the funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月甲辰朔，詔刑罰無輕重悉原之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, on the first day of the first month, jiachen, an edict pardoned all punishments regardless of severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, on the first day of the first month, jiachen, an edict pardoned all crimes regardless of severity.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以尚書令揚州刺史徐羨之為司空、錄尚書事，刺史如故。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yangzhou, was made Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, remaining Governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yangzhou, was made Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 進江州刺史王弘衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, Governor of Jiang, was promoted to Guard General with the privileges of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, Governor of Jiang, was promoted to Guard General with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事傅亮為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Fu Liang, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，有星孛于虛、危。

translations.literal: In the second month on the day bingxu, a comet appeared at the lodge of Emptiness and Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingxu, a comet appeared in the lodges of Emptiness and Rooftop.

sentences.zh: 三月，上不豫，太尉長沙王道憐、司空徐羨之、尚書僕射傅亮、領軍將軍謝晦、護軍將軍檀道濟併入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor was indisposed. The Grand Commandant, Prince of Changsha Daoling; Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works; Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Xie Hui, General of the Guard; and Tan Daoji, General Who Protects the Army—all entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor fell ill. The Grand Commandant, Prince of Changsha Daoling; Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works; Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Xie Hui, General of the Guard; and Tan Daoji, General Who Protects the Army—all entered to attend him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 群臣請祈禱神只，上不許，惟使侍中謝方明以疾告廟而已。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to pray to the spirits, but the Emperor would not permit it. He only had Palace Attendant Xie Fangming report the illness to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to pray to the spirits, but the Emperor refused. He had only Palace Attendant Xie Fangming report the illness to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以廬陵王義真為侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Prince of Luling Yizhen was made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Yizhen, Prince of Luling, was made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, granted privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed Governor of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 己未，上疾瘳，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, the Emperor's illness abated; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, the Emperor recovered; a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙亥，封仇池公楊盛為武都郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on the day yihai, Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, was enfeoffed as King of Wudu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the day yihai, Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, was enfeoffed as King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 五月，上疾甚，召太子，戒之曰：「檀道濟雖有幹略，而無遠志，非如兄韶有難禦之氣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor was gravely ill. He summoned the Crown Prince and admonished him: "Tan Daoji has capacity and strategy, but no distant ambition—unlike my elder brother Shao, who had a spirit hard to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Emperor was gravely ill. He summoned the Crown Prince and warned him: "Tan Daoji has talent and strategy, but no far-reaching ambition—not like my elder brother Shao, who had a spirit hard to withstand.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮當無異圖。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang should harbor no other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang should have no other designs.

sentences.zh: 謝晦屢從征伐，頗識機變，若有異，必此人也。

translations.literal: Xie Hui has often followed on campaigns and knows well how to seize opportunity. If there is a different design, it will surely be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui has often followed on campaign and knows well how to read a moment. If anyone turns against you, it will be he.

sentences.zh: 小卻，可以會稽、江州處之。

translations.literal: When he yields a little, he may be placed in Kuaiji or Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: When he yields a little, place him in Kuaiji or Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 」又為手詔：「朝廷不須復有別府，宰相帶揚州，可置甲士千人。

translations.literal: " He also wrote a hand edict: "The court need not again have separate headquarters. The chief minister who holds Yangzhou may keep one thousand armored men.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote a hand edict: "The court need not again maintain separate headquarters. The chief minister who holds Yangzhou may keep one thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 若大臣中任要，宜有爪牙，以備不祥人者，可以台見留隊給之。

translations.literal: If among the great ministers there are those in important posts who should have claws and teeth to guard against ill-intentioned persons, they may be given guards from the palace garrison on permanent detail.
translations.idiomatic: If any great minister in an important post needs men at his side to guard against ill-intentioned persons, he may be given a guard detail from the palace garrison.

sentences.zh: 有征討，悉配以台見軍隊，行還復舊。

translations.literal: When there are campaigns, they are all to be matched with palace garrison troops; on returning, they revert to the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns arise, they are to be supplied with palace garrison troops; on return, the former arrangement is restored.

sentences.zh: 後世若有幼主，朝事一委任宰相，母后不煩臨朝。

translations.literal: If in later generations there is a young ruler, court affairs are wholly entrusted to the chief minister; the Empress Dowager need not trouble herself to preside at court.
translations.idiomatic: If in later generations there is a young ruler, court affairs are wholly entrusted to the chief minister; the Empress Dowager need not preside at court.

sentences.zh: 仗既不許入台殿門，要重人可詳給班劍。

translations.literal: As weapons are not permitted inside the palace gates, for persons of consequence one may carefully grant ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: As weapons may not enter the palace gates, men of consequence may instead be granted ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，上崩於西殿，時年六十。

translations.literal: " On the day guihai the Emperor died in the West Hall. He was sixty.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day guihai the Emperor died in the West Hall. He was sixty years old.

sentences.zh: 七月己酉，葬丹陽建康縣蔣山初寧陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month on the day jiyou, he was buried at Chuning Mausoleum on Mount Jiang in Jiankang county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on the day jiyou, he was buried at Chuning Mausoleum on Mount Jiang in Jiankang, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 群臣上諡曰武皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: The ministers submitted the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers submitted the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 上清簡寡欲，嚴整有法度，未嘗視珠玉輿馬之飾，後庭無紈綺絲竹之音。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pure and simple, with few desires, stern and orderly in law and measure. He never looked upon adornments of pearls, jade, chariots, or horses, and in the inner quarters there was no silk, brocade, or sound of pipes and strings.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was plain and abstemious, stern and orderly in law. He never looked upon pearls, jade, chariots, or horses as adornments, and in the inner quarters there was no silk, brocade, or music.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷未備音樂，長史殷仲文以為言，帝曰：「日不暇給，且所不解。

translations.literal: At first the court had not yet established music. Chief Clerk Yin Zhongwen spoke of it. The Emperor said: "The day allows no spare time, and besides I do not understand it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court had not yet established music. Chief Clerk Yin Zhongwen raised the matter. The Emperor said: "The day allows no spare time, and besides I do not understand it.

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「屢聽自然解之。

translations.literal: " Yin Zhongwen said: "If you listen often, you will naturally understand it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin Zhongwen said: "Listen often, and you will naturally understand it.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「政以解則好之，故不習耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "It is precisely because if I understood it I would like it, that I do not study it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "It is precisely because understanding it would make me like it that I do not study it.

sentences.zh: 」寧州嘗獻虎魄枕，光色甚麗，價盈百金。

translations.literal: " Ning province once presented an amber pillow; its luster and color were exceedingly lovely, its value exceeding a hundred in gold.
translations.idiomatic: " Ning province once sent an amber pillow of exquisite luster and color, worth more than a hundred in gold.

sentences.zh: 時將北伐，以虎魄療金創，上大悅，命碎分賜諸將。

translations.literal: At the time he was about to campaign north; as amber treats metal wounds, the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it broken apart and distributed to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was about to campaign north. As amber was said to treat metal wounds, the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it broken apart and distributed among the generals.

sentences.zh: 平關中，得姚興從女，有盛寵，以之廢事，謝晦諫，即時遣出。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was pacified he obtained Yao Xing's niece by marriage and favored her greatly. Because of her he neglected affairs of state; Xie Hui remonstrated, and at once he sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Guanzhong he took Yao Xing's niece by marriage and favored her greatly. He neglected affairs of state for her sake; Xie Hui remonstrated, and at once he sent her away.

sentences.zh: 財帛皆在外府，內無私藏。

translations.literal: Treasures and silks were all in the outer treasury; within there was no private store.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures and silks were kept in the outer treasury; he kept no private store within.

sentences.zh: 宋台建，有司奏東西堂施局腳床，金塗釘，上不許。

translations.literal: When the Song palace was built, the relevant offices memorialized that the east and west halls should have cabriole-legged beds with gilt nails. The Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song palace was built, the relevant offices proposed cabriole-legged beds with gilt nails for the east and west halls. The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 使用直腳床，釘用鐵。

translations.literal: Straight-legged beds were to be used; the nails were of iron.
translations.idiomatic: Straight-legged beds were used instead, with iron nails.

sentences.zh: 廣州嘗獻入筒細布，一端八丈，帝惡其精麗勞人，即付有司彈太守，以布還之，並制嶺南禁作此布。

translations.literal: Guang province once presented fine cloth woven in tubes, eight zhang per bolt. The Emperor hated its fineness and beauty as a burden on the people; at once he handed it to the relevant offices to impeach the prefect, returned the cloth, and also ordered that south of the ranges the making of such cloth be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Guang province once sent fine tube-woven cloth, eight zhang per bolt. The Emperor hated its fineness as a burden on the people; at once he had the prefect impeached, returned the cloth, and forbade its manufacture south of the ranges.

sentences.zh: 帝素有熱病，並患金創，末年尤劇，坐臥常須冷物，後有人獻石床，寢之，極以為佳，乃歎曰：「木床且費，而況石邪。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long had feverish illness and also suffered from metal wounds; in his later years these were especially severe. Sitting and lying he constantly required cool things. Later someone presented a stone bed; sleeping on it he found it excellent, yet sighed and said: "A wooden bed already costs enough—how much more a stone one?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long suffered fever and old metal wounds; in his later years these grew especially severe, and sitting or lying he constantly needed something cool. Later someone presented a stone bed. He found it excellent to sleep on, yet sighed and said: "A wooden bed already costs enough—how much more a stone one?

sentences.zh: 」即令毀之。

translations.literal: " At once he ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " At once he ordered it destroyed.

sentences.zh: 制諸主出適，遣送不過二十萬，無錦繡金玉。

translations.literal: He regulated that when princesses went out in marriage, the sending-gifts might not exceed two hundred thousand, and there were to be no brocade, embroidery, gold, or jade.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that when princesses married out, the dowry sent with them might not exceed two hundred thousand, and must include no brocade, embroidery, gold, or jade.

sentences.zh: 內外奉禁，莫不節儉。

translations.literal: Within and without, all observed the prohibition—none were not frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court, all observed the prohibition; none were not frugal.

sentences.zh: 性尤簡易，嘗著連齒木屐，好出神武門內左右逍遙，從者不過十餘人。

translations.literal: His nature was especially plain and easy. He once wore wooden clogs with connected teeth, liked to stroll freely to left and right within the Shenwu Gate, and those following him numbered no more than ten-odd men.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was especially plain and easy. He once wore wooden clogs with connected teeth and liked to stroll freely within the Shenwu Gate, with no more than a dozen men following.

sentences.zh: 時徐羨之住西州，嘗思羨之，便步出西掖門，羽儀絡驛追隨，已出西明門矣。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Xianzhi dwelt in the Western Quarter. Once missing Xianzhi, he simply walked out the Western Side Gate; the imperial guard came in relays in pursuit, and he had already gone out the Western Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Xianzhi lived in the Western Quarter. Once missing Xianzhi, he simply walked out the Western Side Gate; the imperial guard came in relays in pursuit, and he had already passed through the Western Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 諸子旦問起居，入合脫公服，止著裙帽，如家人之禮焉。

translations.literal: When the sons came each morning to inquire after his health, entering the private chamber he removed his official robes and wore only skirt and cap, in the manner of a family.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons came each morning to inquire after his health, he entered the private chamber, removed his official robes, and wore only skirt and cap, as within a family.

sentences.zh: 微時躬耕於丹徒，及受命，耨耜之具頗有存者，皆命藏之，以留於後。

translations.literal: In humble times he had personally plowed at Dantu; after receiving the mandate, quite a few of the hoeing and plow implements remained, and he ordered them all stored away to leave for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: In humble times he had plowed with his own hands at Dantu. After receiving the mandate, quite a few hoes and plows still remained, and he ordered them stored away for posterity.

sentences.zh: 及文帝幸舊宮，見而問焉，左右以實對，文帝色慚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen visited the old palace and saw them and asked, his attendants answered truthfully. Emperor Wen's countenance showed shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen visited the old palace, saw them, and asked, his attendants answered truthfully. Emperor Wen looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 有近侍進曰：「大舜躬耕曆山，伯禹親事土木，陛下不睹列聖之遺物，何以知稼穡之艱難，何以知先帝之至德乎。

translations.literal: A close attendant stepped forward and said: "Great Shun plowed at Mount Li, Lord Yu personally attended to earthworks and timber—Your Majesty, if you do not behold the relics of the successive sages, how will you know the hardship of sowing and reaping, how will you know the utmost virtue of the late Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: A close attendant stepped forward and said: "Great Shun plowed at Mount Li; Lord Yu himself took up earthworks and timber. Your Majesty, if you do not behold the relics of the sages, how will you know the hardship of sowing and reaping, or the late Emperor's utmost virtue?

sentences.zh: 」及孝武大明中，壞上所居陰室，於其處起玉燭殿，與群臣觀之，床頭有土障，壁上掛葛燈籠、麻繩拂，侍中袁顗盛稱上儉素之德，孝武不答，獨曰：「田舍公得此，已為過矣。

translations.literal: " When in the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu they demolished the dark chamber where the late Emperor had lived and on that site raised Jade Candle Hall, and with the ministers viewed it—at the head of the bed was an earthen screen; on the wall hung a hemp lamp-shade and a hemp-rope duster. Palace Attendant Yuan Yi greatly praised the late Emperor's frugal simplicity. Emperor Xiaowu did not reply, but said only: "A rustic landholder who got this would already consider it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu, they demolished the dark chamber where the late Emperor had lived and on that site raised Jade Candle Hall. Viewing it with the ministers, they found an earthen screen at the head of the bed, a hemp lamp-shade and a hemp-rope duster on the wall. Palace Attendant Yuan Yi greatly praised the late Emperor's frugal simplicity. Emperor Xiaowu did not reply, but said only: "A rustic landholder who got this would already consider it excessive.

sentences.zh: 」故能光有天下，克成大業，盛矣哉。

translations.literal: " Thus he could spread his light over the realm and complete the great enterprise—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: " Thus he spread his light over the realm and completed the great enterprise—how grand!

sentences.zh: 永初三年五月癸亥，武帝崩，是日太子即皇帝位，大赦，制服三年，尊皇太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu, on the day guihai in the fifth month, Emperor Wu died. That same day the Crown Prince took the imperial position, proclaimed a general amnesty, observed mourning for three years, and honored the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu, on the day guihai in the fifth month, Emperor Wu died. That same day the Crown Prince took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, entered mourning for three years, and honored the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，以尚書僕射傅亮為中書監、尚書令，司空徐羨之、領軍將軍謝晦及亮輔政。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on the day renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and Director of the Masters of Writing; Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works; Xie Hui, General of the Guard; and Fu Liang formed the regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and Director of the Masters of Writing. Xu Xianzhi, Minister of Works; Xie Hui, General of the Guard; and Fu Liang formed the regency.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太尉長沙王道憐薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Grand Commandant, Prince of Changsha Daoling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, the Grand Commandant, Prince of Changsha Daoling, died.

sentences.zh: 秋九月丁未，有司奏武皇帝配南郊，武敬皇后配北郊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn on the day dingwei, the relevant offices memorialized that Emperor Wu be paired at the Southern Altar and Empress Jing at the Northern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, on the day dingwei, the relevant offices memorialized that Emperor Wu be paired at the Southern Altar and Empress Jing at the Northern Altar.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊午，有星孛于營室。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter on the day wuwu, a comet appeared at Encampment Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on the day wuwu, a comet appeared in Encampment Chamber.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，魏軍克滑台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on the day gengxu, Wei forces captured Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Wei forces captured Huatai.

sentences.zh: 景平元年春正月己亥朔，大赦，改元，文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping, on the first day of the first month in spring, jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed. Civil and military ranks were raised two grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping, on the first day of the first month, jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed. Civil and military ranks were raised two grades.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，祀南郊。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, sacrifice was made at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, sacrifice was made at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 魏軍攻金墉城。

translations.literal: Wei forces attacked Jinyong city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces attacked Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，河南郡失守。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Henan commandery was lost.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Henan commandery fell.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，有星孛於東壁。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, a comet appeared at Eastern Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, a comet appeared in Eastern Wall.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，太皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the second month on the day dingchou, the Grand Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day dingchou, the Grand Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍大將軍大且渠蒙遜、河南鮮卑吐谷渾阿豺並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun, Grand General Who Guards the Army, and A'chai of the Tuyuhun Xianbei in Henan both sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun, Grand General Who Guards the Army, and A'chai of the Tuyuhun Xianbei in Henan both sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，進蒙遜驃騎大將軍，封河西王。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Mengxun was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed as King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Mengxun was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed as King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 以阿豺為安西將軍、沙州刺史，封澆河公。

translations.literal: A'chai was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Sha, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: A'chai was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Sha, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qiaohe.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，孝懿皇后祔葬于興寧陵。

translations.literal: In the third month on the day renyin, Empress Xiaoyi was buried in association at Xingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day renyin, Empress Xiaoyi was buried in association at Xingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 是月，高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏閏四月己未，魏軍克虎牢。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of summer on the day jiwei, Wei forces captured Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on the day jiwei, Wei forces captured Hulao.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，尊所生張夫人為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on the day guiyou, his biological mother Lady Zhang was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day guiyou, his biological mother Lady Zhang was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，赦五歲刑以下。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, those guilty of punishments of five years and below were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, those guilty of punishments of five years and below were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，有星孛於氐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on the day jiwei, a comet appeared at Root.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jiwei, a comet appeared in Root.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏明元皇帝崩。

translations.literal: This year Emperor Mingyuan of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Mingyuan of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the second month in spring, guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the first day of the second month, guisi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 廢南豫州刺史廬陵王義真為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen, Governor of Southern Yu, was deposed as a commoner and moved to Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen, Prince of Luling and Governor of Southern Yu, was deposed as a commoner and exiled to Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大風，天有雲五色，占者以為有兵。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, a great wind blew; the sky had clouds of five colors. Diviners judged that war was portended.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, a great wind blew and the sky showed clouds of five colors. Diviners judged that war was portended.

sentences.zh: 執政使使者誅皇弟義真于新安。

translations.literal: The regents sent envoys to execute the Emperor's younger brother Yizhen at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The regents sent envoys to execute the Emperor's younger brother Yizhen at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 時帝居處所為多乖失。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor's conduct in dwelling and doing was mostly errant and failing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Emperor's conduct in private and in public was mostly errant and unbecoming.

sentences.zh: 夏五月乙酉，皇太后令暴帝過惡，廢為營陽王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer on the day yiyou, the Empress Dowager issued an order exposing the Emperor's faults and deposed him as Prince of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the day yiyou, the Empress Dowager issued an order exposing the Emperor's faults and deposed him as Prince of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 一依漢昌邑、晉海西故事。

translations.literal: Entirely following the precedents of Han's Marquis of Haihun and Jin's Prince of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: This followed entirely the precedents of Han's Marquis of Haihun and Jin's Prince of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 奉迎鎮西將軍宜都王義隆入纂皇統。

translations.literal: They welcomed Yilong, Prince of Yidu and General Who Guards the West, to enter and succeed to the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: They welcomed Yilong, Prince of Yidu and General Who Guards the West, to succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 始徐羨之、傅亮將廢帝，諷王弘、檀道濟求赴國訃，弘等來朝，使中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應。

translations.literal: At first, when Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the Emperor, they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji that they should ask to come for the state mourning. When Hong and the others came to court, they made Central Secretariat Attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their inside contacts.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the Emperor, they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji that they should ask leave to come for the state mourning. When Hong and the others arrived at court, they made Central Secretariat Attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their inside contacts.

sentences.zh: 是旦，道濟、謝晦領兵居前，羨之等隨後，因東掖門開，入自雲龍門，盛等先戒宿衛，莫有禦者。

translations.literal: That morning Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front; Xianzhi and the others followed after. As the Eastern Side Gate opened, they entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate. Sheng and the others had first warned the palace guard, and none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: That morning Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front, with Xianzhi and the others following. As the Eastern Side Gate opened, they entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate. Sheng and the others had already warned the palace guard, and none resisted.

sentences.zh: 時帝于華林園為列肆，親自酤賣，又開瀆聚土，以象破岡埭，與左右引船唱呼，以為歡樂。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor set up rows of shops in the Hualin Park, sold wine himself, and also opened a ditch and piled earth to imitate the Pogang Dam, hauling boats with his attendants while shouting in sport as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He had stalls laid out in Hualin Park and sold wine himself, dug a channel and heaped earth to mimic the Pogang Dam, and with his companions hauled boats and whooped for joy.

sentences.zh: 夕游天泉池，即龍舟而寢。

translations.literal: In the evening he roamed the Tianquan Pool and slept aboard the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: At evening he went to Tianquan Pool and fell asleep on the imperial dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 其朝未興，兵士進，殺二侍者于帝側，傷帝指，扶出東合，就收璽紱。

translations.literal: Before the court had risen, soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the Emperor's side, wounded his finger, helped him out to the eastern wing, and there took the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn soldiers came in, slew two attendants beside him, cut his finger, led him out to the eastern wing, and seized the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 群臣拜辭送於東宮，遂幽于吳郡。

translations.literal: The ministers bowed in farewell and escorted him to the Eastern Palace; he was then confined in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers took leave and sent him to the Eastern Palace, then had him imprisoned in Wu.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦死罪以下。

translations.literal: That day, those sentenced to death and below were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a general pardon was proclaimed for crimes up to and including capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 太后令奉還璽紱，檀道濟入守朝堂。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered that the seal and cord be returned, and Tan Daoji entered to guard the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered the regalia returned, and Tan Daoji took charge of the court hall.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑，徐羨之等使中書舍人邢安泰弑帝于金昌亭。

translations.literal: On day guichou of the sixth month Xu Xianzhi and the others sent Palace Attendant Xing Antai to assassinate the Emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the sixth month Xu Xianzhi and his fellows sent palace attendant Xing Antai to kill the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝有勇力，不即受制，突走出昌門，追以門關踣之致殞，時年十九。

translations.literal: The Emperor was strong and brave and did not submit at once; he broke out through Chang Gate, was pursued, and the gate leaves were slammed on him and killed him. He was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and strong, he would not be taken easily; he burst out through Chang Gate, but pursuers dropped the gate leaves on him and crushed him to death. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：晉自社稷南遷，王綱弛紊，朝權國命，遞回台輔，君道雖存，主威久謝。

translations.literal: The discussion says: From the time Jin moved the altars of state southward, the royal bonds slackened and disordered, and court power and the mandate of the state passed in turn among the terrace ministers; though the way of the ruler endured, sovereign authority had long faded.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: After the Jin court fled south, royal discipline collapsed and real power rotated among the high ministers at court; the throne survived in name, but the ruler's authority was gone.

sentences.zh: 桓溫雄才蓋世，勳高一時，移鼎之業已成，天人之望將改。

translations.literal: Huan Wen's heroic talent overshadowed his age and his merit towered for a season; the work of shifting the tripod was already done, and heaven and men's hopes were about to change.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's genius dominated his generation, and the transfer of the dynasty was within his grasp; heaven and men alike expected a new ruler.

sentences.zh: 自斯以後，帝道彌昏，道子開其禍端，元顯成其釁末。

translations.literal: From then on the imperial way grew ever dimmer: Daozi opened the path of disaster and Yuanxian brought the crisis to its end.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the throne grew ever weaker: Sima Daozi began the ruin and Sima Yuanxian finished it.

sentences.zh: 桓玄乘時藉運，加以先資，革命受終，人無異望。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan seized the moment and rode the tide, aided by prior resources; receiving the mandate in revolution, men harbored no other hope.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan used the times and his family's standing to seize power, and when he took the throne no one expected otherwise.

sentences.zh: 宋武地非齊、晉，眾無一旅，曾不浹旬，夷凶翦暴，誅內清外，功格上下。

translations.literal: Song Wu's territory was not like Qi or Jin, his forces not a single brigade, yet in less than ten days he swept away the fierce and cut down the violent, punished the inner and cleared the outer, his merit reaching high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu ruled no heartland like Qi or Jin and commanded barely a regiment, yet within ten days he destroyed the rebels, pacified the realm, and achieved merit that touched every rank.

sentences.zh: 若夫樂推所歸，謳歌所集，校之魏、晉，可謂收其實矣。

translations.literal: As for the joy of the people and the gathering of songs of praise, compared with Wei and Jin he may be said to have won the reality of it.
translations.idiomatic: Where the people's will and popular acclaim are the measure, beside Wei and Jin he truly earned what they only pretended to hold.

sentences.zh: 然武皇將涉知命，弱嗣方育，顧有慈顏，前無嚴訓。

translations.literal: Yet when the Martial Emperor was about to cross the span of fate, his young heir was still being reared; he had a loving face before him and no stern instruction ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as Emperor Wu neared the end of his life, his young son was still a child, doted on by a tender mother and given no firm discipline.

sentences.zh: 少帝體易染之質，稟可下之姿，外物莫犯其心，所欲必從其志，嶮縱非學而能，危亡不期而集，其至顛沛，非不幸也。

translations.literal: The Lesser Emperor bore a nature easily stained and a disposition fit to be led downward; nothing from without touched his heart, and whatever he desired his will obtained — reckless indulgence learned without study, ruin arriving unlooked for; that he reached such extremity was not misfortune alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao had a nature easily corrupted and a mind ready to sink; outer restraint never touched him, and every whim was satisfied — vice that needed no teaching, downfall that needed no warning. His end was not mere bad luck.
